problem: Orchestrator asked a type-shape question (LineRange start/end vs start/len) to the product owner, who cannot judge it
fix: Ask product/codebase-consequence questions only; decide technical shape from the core visions and record it in docs/plan.md §2

problem: regex for `just bindings` also matched `just bindings-check`; brief required running both, hook forbade it (orchestrator inconsistency)
fix: allow `just bindings` (regenerates from source); restrict only golden-update with a word boundary

problem: `write agent://Main` was treated as a file path and blocked, so peer messaging was impossible
fix: skip URL-shaped targets

problem: oxfmt/oxlint would reformat the generated bindings.ts and fight the generator
fix: ignore src/ipc/bindings.ts in oxfmt and oxlint configs (rework for web slice)

problem: Playwright WebKit cannot launch on Arch (libicu74 etc.); browser project untested
fix: owner decision: install libs / use system WebKit provider / accept jsdom for M1 (product question logged)

problem: The 40-line threshold is now in two places, root clippy.toml and crates/merge-core/clippy.toml. Clippy reads only the nearest clippy.toml, so changing the root value would silently leave merge-core at the old one (vision 2: one constant per tunable).
fix: Add a one-line CP1 comment to both files citing the clippy configuration docs (the nearest clippy.toml shadows its parents, https://doc.rust-lang.org/clippy/configuration.html) and naming the other file, so a reader changing one copy sees the other.

problem: deny.toml reads `unmaintained = "all"`, but the 'warn, not deny' part of the policy lives only in the justfile's `--warn unmaintained`. Anyone running plain `cargo deny check` gets errors that the gate does not.
fix: Add a one-line CP1 comment here saying that cargo-deny v2 config sets only the scope, and that the severity is lowered to warn by `just deny` with `--warn unmaintained`.

problem: The crate doc line includes a roadmap clause ('and later the Tauri commands'), which goes stale the moment M2 lands and is not part of CP3's single-responsibility line.
fix: Change it to `//! Desktop shell: thin Tauri commands and the IPC types exported to the frontend.`

problem: The generated bindings.ts is in this slice's owned set (.omp/run/slices.json) and ipc-contract says it must be committed, but neither M0S0RustSkeleton.patch nor M0S0WebSkeleton.patch contains it. Applying the patches to a clean tree therefore fails `just bindings-check` (diff: No such file), and so `just check` fails.
fix: Regenerate the patch with frontend/src/ipc/bindings.ts included (output of `just bindings`), so the committed artifact matches what bindings-check diffs against.

problem: RS8 denies unwrap/expect/panic only outside #[cfg(test)], but neither clippy.toml sets the test exemptions. With `--all-targets -D warnings`, the first unit or integration test that uses `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!` fails the gate, which pushes later slices into `#[allow]` (itself a should finding).
fix: Add `allow-unwrap-in-tests = true`, `allow-expect-in-tests = true` and `allow-panic-in-tests = true` to both clippy.toml and crates/merge-core/clippy.toml.

problem: The disallowed-methods list covers only read/read_to_string/read_dir/write/File::open/File::create. The other std::fs write functions (`remove_file`, `remove_dir_all`, `create_dir_all`, `copy`, `rename`) compile clean in merge-core, so PM1's "no std::fs" is only partly enforced.
fix: Add the remaining std::fs mutating functions to disallowed-methods, or add a `grep -rE 'std::(fs|process)' crates/merge-core/src` failure to scripts/arch-check.sh as one exhaustive detector.

problem: Clippy does not merge a crate clippy.toml with the root one, so `too-many-lines-threshold = 40` is duplicated in two files. Editing the root value silently leaves merge-core on the old threshold, which violates vision 2 (one constant per tunable).
fix: Have scripts/arch-check.sh fail when the two files' `too-many-lines-threshold` lines differ, so the duplication is enforced rather than remembered.

problem: `cargo tree` without `--target all --all-features` sees only host-target, default-feature edges. A `cfg(target_os = "macos")` or optional `yamt-merge-core` dep in gitio would pass arch-check on Linux.
fix: Use `cargo tree --package "$1" --edges normal --target all --all-features --prefix none` in normal_deps.

problem: `--no-tests=warn` lets `just test` stay green if a workspace stops compiling any tests (for example a broken filter or a removed tests dir). It is only needed while the skeleton has zero tests.
fix: Drop `--no-tests=warn` in the first slice that adds a Rust test, so the recipe matches §7's `cargo nextest run --workspace`.

problem: Cross-slice issue; the file belongs to M0S0RustSkeleton. The web-* recipes call `pnpm -C frontend vitest run` / `oxlint` / `eslint` directly instead of the package scripts named in brief line 8. As a result `just check` runs the browser project, which cannot launch WebKit on this machine, and fails. It also skips `--max-warnings 0`, so the gate and `pnpm lint` are two definitions that drift.
fix: Change the recipes to `(frontend "lint")`, `(frontend "typecheck")`, `(frontend "test")`, `(frontend "sfc-order")` and `(frontend "fmt:check")`, so frontend/package.json is the one place each web gate is defined.

problem: `types: ["vite/client", "node"]` applies to all of src/. Webview code under src/editor or src/ui can use `process.env` or `Buffer` and still typecheck, then fail at runtime. `setTimeout` is also typed as returning `NodeJS.Timeout` instead of `number`.
fix: Split the config: an app tsconfig for src/** with `types: ["vite/client"]`, and a node tsconfig for scripts/** and vite.config.ts with `types: ["node"]`, both referenced from tsconfig.json (the stock vite vue-ts layout). Point vue-tsc at both, e.g. with `-b`.

problem: The framework-free fence blocks only the exact `vue` specifier. `import { ref } from "@vue/reactivity"`, `@vue/runtime-core` or `vue/…` subpaths in src/editor, src/model or src/connectors pass lint, which breaks PM3 and decision 22.
fix: Add `"vue/*"` and `"@vue/*"` to the PM3 pattern group next to `@vueuse/*` and `@tauri-apps/*`.

problem: The ui override's internal group is `["../editor/internal/*", "**/internal/*"]`. It is missing the bare `**/internal` entry that the base, ipc and editor groups all have, so `import … from "../editor/internal"` (which resolves to internal/index.ts) passes lint from src/ui.
fix: Add `"**/internal"` to the ui override's internal group so all four PM5 groups have the same shape.

problem: `layoutRulesOff` turns off every eslint-plugin-vue rule whose meta.type is "layout". The brief says flat/recommended only, and this change to the Vue ruleset is not in the accepted deviations.
fix: Either remove `layoutRulesOff`, or keep it and report it in deviations_from_brief, naming the oxfmt conflict that motivated it so the orchestrator can record it.

problem: log.ts exports seven names. LogLevel, LogFields, LogForward and Log have no importer anywhere in src/; only createLog, LogEntry (used by the test) and log are consumed.
fix: Drop `export` from LogLevel, LogFields, LogForward and Log; keep LogEntry, createLog and log.

problem: The forward-failure path builds the `[error] … {…}` line by hand, so the line format exists both here and in mirror().
fix: Replace it with `mirror({ level: "error", event: "log.forward_failed", fields: { reason: String(error) } })`.

problem: src/ipc, src/ui and src/editor already contain real files, so their .gitkeep files do nothing. Brief line 6 asked for ipc/.gitkeep only if bindings.ts was absent.
fix: Delete .gitkeep from src/ipc, src/ui and src/editor; keep it only in the still-empty model/, connectors/ and fixtures/.

problem: Statements that are not classified are skipped silently. A composable call such as `const store = useAppStore()` or `useMergeController(...)` (VU9/VU11, the two composables v0 components will call) placed after function declarations or lifecycle hooks passes `pnpm sfc-order`.
fix: In calleeSection, classify any Identifier callee matching `/^use[A-Z]/` as "state", so composables join the ref/useTemplateRef section and their misplacement is reported.

problem: VU2 orders all "lifecycle hooks" and watch effects, but CALLEE_SECTIONS lists only six hooks and two watchers. A misplaced onActivated, onDeactivated, onErrorCaptured, onRenderTracked, onRenderTriggered, onServerPrefetch, watchPostEffect, watchSyncEffect or shallowReactive after a function declaration is not reported.
fix: Add the missing Vue lifecycle hooks to "lifecycle", watchPostEffect and watchSyncEffect to "watch", and shallowReactive to "state".

problem: LogForward is typed `(entry) => void`, so an async forward (the planned forward is `commands.log`, which returns a Promise) type-checks. Its rejection then escapes as an unhandled promise rejection, skips the `log.forward_failed` path, and breaks the 'never throws' guarantee for the only real forward.
fix: Type LogForward as `(entry: LogEntry) => Promise<unknown> | void`. When forward returns a Promise, attach `.catch((error) => mirror({ level: "error", event: "log.forward_failed", ... }))`, and keep the try/catch for synchronous throws.

problem: The throwing-forward test mocks console.error but never asserts on it. Emptying the catch body at log.ts:52, which is the exact path rework item 3 changed, would leave the suite green.
fix: Assert that console.error was called with '[error] apply.chunk {id: 1}' and then '[error] log.forward_failed {reason: "Error: ipc down"}'.

problem: No test covers the IPC8 debug gate. Deleting `level === "debug" && !import.meta.env.DEV`, or dropping the `!`, keeps both tests passing, even though production would then forward debug entries over IPC (or dev would lose them).
fix: Add a log.test.ts case that uses `vi.stubEnv("DEV", false)` to show `log.debug` mirrors but does not forward, and `vi.stubEnv("DEV", true)` to show it forwards once, with `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` in afterEach.

problem: The ui→model group matches only `../model` and `../model/*`. A component in a ui subdirectory importing `../../model/x` passes lint, while the bindings and internal groups use the depth-independent `**/` form.
fix: Change the group to `["**/model", "**/model/**"]`, matching the shape of the `**/ipc/bindings` and `**/internal` groups.

problem: The script that gates `just check` has no automated test, only the manual one-off proof from acceptance. A regression that makes classify return undefined for every statement (for example a compiler-sfc or typescript API change) turns the gate into a silent pass on every file.
fix: Have firstViolation take `(file, text)`, export it, and add `scripts/check-sfc-order.test.ts` to the node Vitest project. Cover one in-order SFC, one with function-before-computed (asserting the reported line), and one with a composable after a lifecycle hook.

problem: `String(error)` itself throws a TypeError when forward throws a value with no toString (for example `Object.create(null)`), so that error escapes `emit` despite the never-throw contract.
fix: Use `error instanceof Error ? error.message : typeof error` for `reason`.

problem: Orchestrator asked the verifier to tamper a file as a smoke step; the verifier is read-only by design and the ownership hook blocked it
fix: Smoke recipes that mutate files belong to the implementer's acceptance; verifier recipes are read-only commands only (clarify in skill://verification and skill://orchestrate)

problem: Gate D question used internal vocabulary invented during the session (proposal ids P1-P13, rule ids OR1/L2, tool names like tsgolint, 'fence probes'); the human had read none of the process and could not answer
fix: Every message and question to the human is self-contained plain language: no ids, no AI-invented terms, no tool names unless the human introduced them; assume the human read nothing of the thought process; each option states what changes for the human in one sentence

problem: Board listed the Rust merge engine (M0) as next; human directed: build the frontend window first, no Rust backend yet, editor plus toolbar buttons that do nothing yet
fix: Board gains an early-M1 section ahead of M0; inert buttons are explicit human scope, not unfinished work

problem: Human product direction: dark theme; the whole window should look like a JetBrains IDE (from memory, not pixel-exact); file list shows only the sample file until real loading exists
fix: Recorded as decision row 24 in docs/plan.md §2; briefs carry the JetBrains-dark look

problem: Session 2 was started in frontend/ instead of the repo root; project settings (.omp/config.yml modelRoles implementer/reviewer/verifier) are loaded only from the process cwd, so every project agent failed at spawn with a misleading 'No model selected' error (5 spawns, <1s each). Proven: `omp --model=@implementer -p` works from repo root, 'Model "@implementer" not found' from frontend/
fix: Re-hydrate step checks the session cwd is the repo root before any spawn (proposal for next retro: orchestrate §0 line, or a session-start hook that warns when cwd != repo root)

problem: Brief and VU15 fixed single-word component names (Sidebar, Toolbar, Banner) that the configured Vue linter rule multi-word-component-names rejects; the implementer hit lint failure mid-slice
fix: Renamed to FileList, MergeToolbar, WarningBanner in VU15, architecture 5.4, project-map, brief; lint rule kept. Proposal for retro: briefs that name new files are checked against the lint config before Gate A

problem: The only thing that drops every acyclic file's singleton SCC is the `edge === undefined` early return. It reads like a defensive guard, so a reader has to reverse-engineer Tarjan output to learn that 'first member has no edge into its component' means 'not a cycle'.
fix: Extract a named predicate, e.g. `function cycleEntry(members, graph): Edge | undefined`, or filter `stronglyConnected(graph)` explicitly with `isCycle` (size > 1 or self-edge) before mapping, so the cycle/non-cycle decision is stated by a name.

problem: The `?raw` test imports `./theme.css?raw`, which matches no rule and no known file with or without stripping. It still passes if QUERY_SUFFIX stripping (fences.ts:21,150) is deleted, so query stripping has no test that fails without it.
fix: Keep the brief's non-violating shape but make stripping matter: add a second case, e.g. a ui file importing `../model?raw`, expecting PM2 (it is missed without stripping because `src/model?raw` is not inside `src/model`), or assert that a `?raw` import of a known file creates the expected edge.

problem: FRAMEWORK_FREE_MODULES is a membership set written as `Record<string, true>` + `Object.hasOwn`, while the same file uses `ReadonlySet<string>` for the same kind of check at line 141.
fix: Declare `const FRAMEWORK_FREE_MODULES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["editor", "model", "connectors"])` and test it with `.has(module)`.

problem: Any resolved path with an `internal` segment outside src/ is reported as PM5. Probed: src/ui/sample.ts importing `../../fixtures/internal/a.txt?raw` gives a PM5 violation, even though under the brief a module is only a first directory under src/.
fix: Bind `const targetModule = MODULE_OF.exec(target)?.[1]` and report PM5 only when `targetModule !== undefined && targetModule !== module && target.split("/").includes("internal")`. Then add a test showing that a ui `?raw` import from `../../fixtures/internal/x.txt` is allowed.

problem: The `?raw` test still passes if QUERY_SUFFIX stripping is deleted: `src/editor/theme.css?raw` violates nothing with or without the query, so nothing proves 'query suffixes are stripped before resolving'.
fix: Add an assertion where the query would hide a violation, e.g. `src/ui/s.ts` with `import "../model?raw"` expecting one PM2 on `src/ui/s.ts`. Keep the existing no-violation case.

problem: The whole suite still passes if `.ts` or `.vue` is removed from RESOLVE_SUFFIXES (fences.ts:23). The only cycle fixture uses `./b`→`b/index.ts` and an explicit `../a.ts`, so the most common form, an extensionless sibling `./b`→`b.ts`, could stop producing cycle edges without any test failing.
fix: Make the cycle fixture `src/model/a.ts` (`import "./b"`) ↔ `src/model/b.ts` (`import "./a"`), or add that as a second case, plus one cycle edge that resolves through `.vue` (e.g. `src/ui/A.vue` ↔ `src/ui/b.ts` via `./A`). Expect exactly one PM5 per cycle.

problem: `text-white` here and in FileList.vue:21 takes its colour from Tailwind's default theme (`--color-white`), not from the yamt palette. Because style.css never resets the defaults, every stock Tailwind colour (`red-500`, `zinc-*`, …) is still available as a second palette next to `@theme`.
fix: Add `--color-*: initial;` at the top of the `@theme static` block and a `--color-on-primary` token. Then use `text-on-primary` in both places, so the `@theme` block is the only source of colours.

problem: Looking up a language needs `Object.hasOwn` plus a ternary (pane.ts:96-99), and the result goes into a local named `language` that holds a factory, not a language name.
fix: Make `LANGUAGES` a `ReadonlyMap<string, () => Extension>` and inline `(pane.language === null ? undefined : LANGUAGES.get(pane.language))?.() ?? []`. Alternatively, rename the local to `languageExtension`.

problem: `PaneKind` is exported, but nothing outside pane.ts uses it: index.ts passes string literals.
fix: Remove `export` from `type PaneKind` until a second module needs it.

problem: The 'scroll each .cm-scroller to the bottom, then read the last gutter line' probe cannot tell whether a pane scrolls on its own. CodeMirror renders a 1000px margin beyond the visible area, so all 81 lines (about 1475px) are in the DOM at scrollTop 0 and lastGutterLine would be [81,76,76] even if a scroller never moved. Independent per-pane scrolling therefore rests only on the screenshot.
fix: Extend the DOM-facts probe to record each scroller's scrollHeight > clientHeight and its scrollTop after the scroll (expect > 0), and paste that into the evidence.

problem: Only 3 unchanged lines separate the remote-only subtotal change from the discount conflict, and the conflict from the remote-only tax change. At gap ≥ 3 (the 'loose grouping' the architecture open question considers) both remote-only chunks would be absorbed into the conflict, and the sample would lose its 'remote changes a different function' shape.
fix: Move one unchanged function (e.g. summary or createCart) between subtotal and discount, and another between discount and tax, so the four shapes stay separate for any plausible gap.

problem: Respawning an implementer under its finished name (isolated agents cannot be revived) got the task name suffixed `-2`, which slices.json did not list, so the ownership hook had no entry for the live agents until the orchestrator rewrote the registry after spawning; the registry hook also rejects keeping the finished names because their globs overlap
fix: Rework spawns use an explicit new name (e.g. `M1WindowShellR1`) and slices.json is rewritten with only the live names before spawning; proposal for retro: one line in orchestrate step 6

problem: A broadcast to all agents (to tell the two live implementers to retry) also woke four idle reviewers, briefly running six agents against the cap of two; they were stopped within seconds and did nothing
fix: Message live agents by name, never broadcast while idle agents exist

problem: Isolated agents run in a copy of the last commit, and the ownership hook reads .omp/run/slices.json from that copy (resolve(cwd, ...)); a registry change that is written but not committed before spawning is invisible to the agents, so both rework agents were blocked on every edit and one aborted (about 2 minutes lost)
fix: Orchestrate step 3: write slices.json AND commit it before spawning isolated agents; proposal for retro: the slice-registry or task-fanout hook warns when slices.json differs from HEAD at spawn time

problem: The deadline only covers git's own exit: stdout/stderr are joined afterwards with no time limit. `checkout -m -- <path>` runs the user's post-checkout hook, whose stdout goes to stderr; if that hook starts a background process that keeps stderr open, checkout_merge blocks indefinitely despite GIT_TIMEOUT.
fix: Have the reader threads send their results over an `mpsc` channel and receive with `recv_timeout(deadline - now)`, returning `Error::Timeout` when the shared deadline passes.

problem: No test covers the brief's rule that a non-`blob` type returns UnexpectedOutput and leaves the reader usable. If a regression returned before `read_content_and_newline`, the cat-file stream would fall out of sync and every later `read` would fail, and no test would notice.
fix: Extend test 5: read the HEAD commit oid (fixture `git rev-parse HEAD` → `Oid::parse`), assert `UnexpectedOutput { command: "cat-file", .. }`, then assert the next `read(&entries[0].oid)` still returns BASE.

problem: find_git_on_path accepts relative PATH entries: an empty entry gives `git`, which is looked up on PATH again, and `bin` gives `bin/git`. Command then resolves these against current_dir(root) (std documents this as platform-specific), not the directory where git was found, so the binary that runs may not be the one 'resolved once' in discover.
fix: Skip entries where `!dir.is_absolute()` in the PATH loop so Repo.git is always an absolute path.

problem: The once-per-path removal record is hidden inside the per-stage loop as `enumerate()` + `if index == 0`, so a reader has to infer the 'first record of each path' structure from an index check (principles §2, vision 1).
fix: Make the dedupe loop keep the first entry of each path (`firsts: Vec<&StageEntry>`), then write `for first in firsts { push_removal_record(&mut input, first); for entry in entries.iter().filter(|e| e.path == first.path) { push_stage_record(&mut input, entry); } }`.

problem: The stdin writer thread is created with `child.stdin.take().zip(stdin).map(|(mut pipe, bytes)| thread::spawn(..))`. Option::zip is an obscure combinator for a Rust-beginner reader, and it hides the plain rule 'spawn a writer only when there is input' (vision 1, principles §2).
fix: Use `let writer = if let (Some(mut pipe), Some(bytes)) = (child.stdin.take(), stdin) { Some(thread::spawn(move || pipe.write_all(&bytes))) } else { None };`.

problem: Doc comments on non-merge-core items restate names or fields, which is outside CP2 (merge-core public items only): blob.rs:9 (BlobReader), repo.rs:14 (Repo), entry.rs:10 (Oid: SHA1_HEX_LEN and SHA256_HEX_LEN already say it), entry.rs:36 (Stage numbering, repeated by index_number), entry.rs:63 (StageEntry), entry.rs:111 (index_info), run.rs:12 (Access: the match says it), run.rs:43 (run). run.rs:108 explains what `None` means instead of the type saying it. entry.rs:75 is a git-format fact without a reference.
fix: Delete the restating doc comments. Return a named enum `Waited { Exited(ExitStatus), TimedOut }` from wait_or_kill in place of the run.rs:108 comment. Keep entry.rs:75 as a CP1 `//` line citing git-ls-files(1) `-z` output.

problem: The test-11 reap check reads /proc/self/task/*/children with unwrap, so `cargo nextest run -p yamt-gitio` panics on macOS, which the brief names as a target platform (plan: 'Also runs on: macOS (arm64)').
fix: Mark child_pids_of_this_process and its final assert_eq with `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`, so the Timeout and elapsed-time assertions still run on macOS.

problem: The GitFailed Display shows the status as Debug (`exit status Some(128)`) and appends git's raw stderr, including its trailing newline, so the user-facing message ends in `\n` and shows Rust Option syntax.
fix: Store `stderr.trim_end()` in run.rs:67 and render the status with `status.map_or_else(|| "killed by signal".to_owned(), |code| format!("exit status {code}"))` in the #[error] arguments.

problem: Each git subcommand name is written twice: as the error label (`LS_FILES` here, `CAT_FILE` in blob.rs:7, `"rev-parse"` in repo.rs:27) and again as a separate literal in the argv in repo.rs:23/41/46, so the two can drift apart (vision 2).
fix: Use the same const in both places, e.g. `self.command(Access::Read, &[LS_FILES, "-u", "-z"])` with the const made pub(crate), or move the error label next to the argv in repo.rs.

problem: `triple()` has no path that gives both sides the same edit. [INFERENCE] So BothSame chunks in proptests 3 and 7 come almost only from both sides happening to set the same new last line, a few percent of cases and nearly always at EOF. A BothSame classification bug for mid-file regions, or for regions merged through the gap, would rarely be generated.
fix: Add a `shared` arm to `triple()` that applies one common edit list to base, then separate extra edit lists per side. Also run proptests 3 and 7 on `(base, local, local)`, where every two-sided region must be BothSame.

problem: Proptest 4 checks `.iter().all(..)` over the chunk list. It would still pass if `compute_chunks` returned no chunks at all, so on its own it does not show that the changed side's edits are reported.
fix: In each leg, also assert `chunks.is_empty() == (changed_side == base)`, e.g. `prop_assert_eq!(kinds(base, base, remote).is_empty(), remote == base)`.

problem: The heart of architecture step 4 is called `SideDiff::map` (called as `local.map(&region.base)`, line 94). A TS-proficient reader takes that for Array.map. Its helper `side_line(preceding_hunks: usize, ..)` receives a partition count, so the reader has to work out the `<` (start) vs `<=` (end) asymmetry from names alone.
fix: Rename `map` to `map_base_to_side`, the name architecture §3.1 step 4 uses. Rename `starting_within` to `starting_at_or_before_end` so the `<=` boundary rule (an insertion at the region end belongs to the region) is in the name.

problem: Each match arm (lines 16, 19, 21) rebuilds a `Range<u32>` from a typed `LineRange` with `x.start.0..x.end().0`. The tail at line 28 slices base lines a second way (`.get(next as usize..)`), so one function uses two slicing idioms.
fix: Use `lines_in` for the tail too (`lines_in(&base_lines, &(next_base_line..len))`). Or have a private helper take `(start, len)` so the arms read `lines_in(&local_lines, chunk.local.start.0, chunk.local.len)`.

problem: `Options` and `DEFAULT_GAP` are inputs to `compute_chunks` but live in `chunk.rs`, the module for output types. A reader looking for what `gap` controls opens the wrong file first.
fix: Move `Options`, its `Default` impl and `DEFAULT_GAP` into `compute.rs` next to `compute_chunks`, their only consumer, and re-export them from there in lib.rs.

problem: `closed_pipe()` is now defined twice with identical bodies, here and in blob.rs:78, because the rework copied it from blob.rs instead of sharing it (vision 2).
fix: Make run.rs's `closed_pipe` `pub(crate)`, import it in blob.rs next to `argv` (`use crate::run::{argv, closed_pipe};`), and delete the copy in blob.rs.

problem: The nested generic `Receiver<io::Result<Vec<u8>>>` is spelled out three times (run.rs:117, 131, 132), which a Rust-beginner reader has to re-parse at each signature (vision 1).
fix: Add `type PipeOutput = Receiver<io::Result<Vec<u8>>>;` next to `Waited` and use it in read_on_thread and receive_output.

problem: [0.1] The invariant 'every chunk of (base, local, local) is BothSame' is asserted twice, at lines 224 and 280. Neither test name describes it, while proptest 4's local==remote leg (line 249) asserts the weaker `!contains(Conflict)`. This breaks the original brief's 'each invariant is its own named test'.
fix: Replace line 249 with `prop_assert!(both_changed.iter().all(|kind| *kind == ChunkKind::BothSame))` and delete lines 224 and 280. Proptests 3 and 7 then keep only the `for triple in [triple, shared]` loop.

problem: [0.1] The one saved seed (`base: "", local: "x", remote: ""`) came from the reverted item-3 mutation (`compute_chunks` returning `Vec::new()`), not from a failure of real code. The new file records debris from a throwaway run.
fix: Delete the untracked file before committing. Let proptest recreate it only when real code fails.

problem: git add keeps a resolve-undo record and `git checkout -m` rebuilds the conflict from it, so a finish-then-reset test passes even when session captures stages lazily; the RK1 proving test as registered cannot catch the bug it exists for (found by the 0.2 implementer).
fix: RK1 test row: clear the resolve-undo record (`git update-index --clear-resolve-undo`) after finish before asserting reset restores the captured stages.

problem: No risk row for non-regular files: a submodule conflict (mode 160000) made `MergeSession::open` fail for the whole merge, and a symlink conflict (mode 120000) would be decoded as text and written back as a regular file.
fix: Add a risk row (owner session: mode-based unsupported reason; test: open on a merge with a submodule/symlink conflict lists it as unsupported and the other files stay usable).

problem: If `restore_stages` succeeds and `checkout_merge` then fails (timeout, git error), the index is unmerged again but the status stays Resolved, so files() shows Resolved and remaining() undercounts compared with `ls-files -u`.
fix: Set the status to Unresolved right after `restore_stages` returns Ok, before calling `checkout_merge`.

problem: Decoding stops at the first side that fails and runs Binary → TooLarge → NonUtf8 per side, so a Latin-1 base with a NUL-containing local is reported NonUtf8 rather than Binary as the brief's "any side with a NUL → Binary" rule says. Every fixture fails identically on all three sides, so no test pins the cross-side order.
fix: Run each check across all three sides in the brief's order (NUL probe on every side, then UTF-8, then size, or state the chosen order in the brief), and add a decode unit test whose sides fail differently, e.g. a non-UTF-8 base with a binary local.

problem: The "local when base is empty" EOL branch is never exercised: no test loads an add/add file with CRLF, so replacing `eol_source` with `&texts.base` keeps every test green, and an add/add CRLF file would then report Lf (RK5).
fix: Give the ADD_ADD fixture CRLF line breaks, or add a test that loads a CRLF add/add file and asserts `eol == Eol::CrLf`.

problem: Reset is only proven after finish on a modify/modify file. An add/add file (no base stage in the replayed index-info) and a reset of a file that was never finished (which the brief says must work) have no test, so a regression in either path goes unnoticed.
fix: Parameterise the reset test over a modify/modify and an add/add ConflictFile, and add a case that resets without finishing first; each asserts `ls-files -u` is identical and the worktree contains `<<<<<<<`.

problem: The TooLarge fixture is 8 MiB + 1 byte, so changing `>` to `>=` in decode_side still passes; the size boundary is not pinned the way the NUL window is.
fix: In decode.rs tests, assert that `MAX_TEXT_BYTES` bytes decode Ok and `MAX_TEXT_BYTES + 1` bytes give TooLarge.

problem: hash_object ignores the child's exit status and silently skips the write when stdin is missing, so a failing `git hash-object` yields Ok("") instead of an error.
fix: Check `output.status.success()` and return `Error::GitFailed` with the stderr, as git_ok does.

problem: finish (line 126) and reset (line 139) each look the path up twice: first with file(), then with file_mut() at the end. The second lookup's UnknownPath branch can never fire, but a reader still has to work out why it cannot fail.
fix: Replace the file()/file_mut() pair with one free fn `find_file(files: &mut [FileState], path: &str) -> Result<&mut FileState>`. Call it once per method as `let file = find_file(&mut self.files, path)?;` and set `file.status` directly; the disjoint borrows of `self.files` and `self.repo` compile.

problem: The lookup calls display_path(), which allocates a new String for every file it compares on each load/finish/reset, but only to test equality.
fix: In the lookup, compare without allocating: `file.path.to_string_lossy() == path` (Cow<str> == &str). Keep display_path() only for building the DTOs.

problem: The comment states an external git fact (checkout -m refuses delete/modify paths) but gives no source, so a reader cannot check it or tell which git version it applies to.
fix: Add the source on the same line, e.g. `(git builtin/checkout.c checkout_merged; observed on git 2.56)`.

problem: hash_object never checks the exit status and silently skips writing when stdin is missing, so a failed `git hash-object` returns Ok("") or the hash of empty input instead of an Err. That is a fake fallback in a library whose contract is to return Result.
fix: Turn a missing stdin into an error with `child.stdin.take().ok_or_else(|| std::io::Error::other("hash-object stdin not piped"))?`, and return Error::GitFailed when `!output.status.success()`, as git_ok does.

problem: IPC6 still says `FileEntry.supported = false` with a reason, which contradicts this slice's decided `unsupported: Option<UnsupportedReason>`. Also, docs/architecture.md:221 still lists a `blobs: BlobReader` field and :235 says load reads blobs, which the accepted decode-at-open deviation made stale. These are orchestrator-owned files.
fix: The orchestrator should change IPC6 to `FileEntry.unsupported` set to a reason, drop `blobs: BlobReader` from architecture §3.3 line 221, and change the load comment on line 235 to `decoded at open; compute_chunks`.

problem: `file.texts()?;` throws its value away and works only as a guard, so the line reads as a leftover.
fix: Rename texts() to require_text() so both call sites read as a guard: `let texts = file.require_text()?;` in load and `file.require_text()?;` in finish.

problem: A beginner has to decode the `match` with a guard plus a `Some(_) | None` arm before seeing it is just 'same path as the last group?'.
fix: Use an edition-2024 let-chain: `if let Some((path, stages)) = groups.last_mut() && *path == entry.path { stages.insert(entry) } else { … }`.

problem: `reset` on a Submodule file always returns `Err(Git(..))`. After `restore_stages`, `has_both_sides()` is true, so `checkout_merge` runs, and git aborts with `fatal: unable to read blob object` (exit 128, seen in the /tmp probe on git 2.56). This happens whether or not the file was resolved outside the app, although the brief says reset works for every file. Index and status do end up correct.
fix: Skip `checkout_merge` for gitlink stages too (e.g. guard on `has_both_sides() && !has_mode(SUBMODULE_MODE)`, with git's message cited on the comment line), and add a test that resets the submodule file from NON_REGULAR_NEXT_TO_TEXT and asserts Ok plus `ls-files -u` identical.

problem: `succeeded(args, output)` is named like a bool predicate, but it returns the stdout bytes or a GitFailed error, so `succeeded(&HASH_OBJECT_ARGS, …)?` at its call sites reads as a check, not as the source of `stdout`.
fix: Rename it to `stdout_or_failure` (or `require_success`) so `let stdout = stdout_or_failure(&HASH_OBJECT_ARGS, output)?;` says what it returns.

problem: Reset of a symlink conflict runs `git checkout -m`, which exits 0 but rewrites the link target to conflict-marker text (probe, git 2.56). Reachable only if the user resolved the symlink outside the app (finish refuses unsupported files).
fix: When v0.1 adds take-local/take-remote for unsupported files, decide whether reset of a symlink skips checkout -m like gitlinks; add a test then.

problem: Planned a slice for the default `task` agent, which is disabled in this project's settings; the spawn failed preflight. Non-Rust, non-web work (git archaeology, shell scripts) has no matching implementer type.
fix: Either state in skill://orchestrate which agent takes language-neutral slices (rust-impl was used for 0.3'), or add a small agent definition for data/script slices at the next retro.

problem:
RK13 as written ('for conflict-free triples, output == git merge-file -p') is unachievable: imara-diff and git's xdiff align ambiguous runs of repeated lines differently, so yamt can see no conflict where git does (shrunk: base "x
z
x
z
x
x
x
x
"). Orchestrator reformulated: equality when BOTH yamt and git (--diff-algorithm=histogram) are conflict-free, plus a non-vacuous floor and printed disagreement counts.
fix: Update the RK13 row's proving-test text to the both-clean formulation at the next retro.

problem: The deterministic sample prints `only_git_conflicts` but never bounds it. If the chunk model regressed so that yamt auto-applies triples git calls conflicting (the dangerous direction of RK13), both tests would still pass and the problem would show only as a changed count in --no-capture output (the implementer's open risk at :191).
fix: In the deterministic test, also assert that only_git_conflicts stays under a named ceiling constant (e.g. MAX_ONLY_GIT_CONFLICT_PERCENT = 1, 0 of 512 today). That turns the open risk into a detector without touching the accepted equality property.

problem: The only DIFF test changes JSON content (Conflict → BothSame), so a golden run that compared parsed JSON instead of bytes would pass every test, even though the contract says `compare bytes`. The line-ending and line-count hint branches of first_difference are also never exercised.
fix: Add a case that rewrites expected.json as classified.replace('\n', "\r\n"), same JSON with different bytes, and assert exit 1 with `DIFF second: same lines, different line endings`.

problem: The Error enum hand-writes Display, From and an empty `impl std::error::Error` (line 59) instead of `#[derive(thiserror::Error)]`. About 45 lines of boilerplate a Rust beginner has to read, and `source()` returns None for Read/Write/Session/Json, so the cause chain is lost. thiserror is already a workspace dependency and is locked for yamt-session.
fix: Orchestrator adds `thiserror.workspace = true` to crates/cli/Cargo.toml. Then the enum derives thiserror::Error, with `#[error("...")]` per variant, `#[from]` on Session/Json and `#[source]` on the io errors; the manual Display/From/Error impls are deleted.

problem: first_difference uses str::lines(), which ignores a final newline. An expected.json that differs only by a missing trailing newline is reported as `same lines, different line endings`, which points the reader at CRLF.
fix: Before the line loop, check `expected.ends_with('\n') != actual.ends_with('\n')` and return a `trailing newline differs` hint.

problem: cli's Error is hand-written: about 45 lines of Display, an empty `impl std::error::Error` and two From impls. Every other crate (gitio, session, conflict-repo) uses `#[derive(thiserror::Error)]`, so cli sets up a second error convention. The empty impl also drops `source()`, so the io and serde errors are not chained.
fix: Orchestrator adds `thiserror.workspace = true` to crates/cli/Cargo.toml. It is already a workspace dependency in Cargo.lock, so no new crate enters the build. Then replace the manual impls with `#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]` plus `#[error(..)]`/`#[from]`, as in crates/session/src/lib.rs.

problem: `std::env::args()` panics if any argument is not valid Unicode (std docs), so a non-UTF-8 path given to classify/scan/golden/fixture aborts with a panic. The user should get `yamt-cli: <message>` and exit 2.
fix: Collect `std::env::args_os().skip(1).map(OsString::into_string).collect::<Result<Vec<String>, _>>()` and turn the `Err` into a usage error, e.g. by passing it into run or letting `args::parse` take the `OsString`s.

problem: `expected_json(case)` returns the JSON freshly computed from the case, but mismatch binds it as `let actual = expected_json(case)?` (line 78), right next to `expected` (the file's bytes). The reader has to open the function to learn which side is which.
fix: Rename it to `computed_json` (or `chunks_json_of`) so line 78 reads `let actual = computed_json(case)?` and update() writes `computed_json(case)?` into expected.json.

problem: The generic file helpers `read_text` and `read_error` live in the golden-case module. classify.rs:5 therefore imports `crate::case::read_text`, even though classify has nothing to do with cases.
fix: Move `read_text` and `read_error` to lib.rs next to `print`/`print_lines` (the crate's shared I/O helpers) and import them from `crate::`.

problem: The hint text hard-codes "expected.json", while the file name is already the `EXPECTED_FILE` const in case.rs:6, so the name is written in two places (vision 2).
fix: Make `EXPECTED_FILE` pub(crate) and build the hint with `format!("{EXPECTED_FILE} is missing")`.

problem: Git still reads the user's own attributes and ignore files: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/attributes` and `~/.config/git/ignore` are the defaults for core.attributesFile and core.excludesFile, and they apply even with GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null. A probe with `* -merge` in XDG attributes gave 'Cannot merge binary files', and the worktree had no conflict markers. A matching ignore pattern would make `git add -- <path>` fail.
fix: Add `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -c core.excludesFile=/dev/null` to the `g()` options next to `core.autocrlf=false`.

problem: The README says remote has 241 lines, but `wc -l remote.ts` prints 240. The counting rule is stated only in tests/golden/README.md, so someone checking this case's README alone sees a mismatch.
fix: Add a note to the Lines entry, e.g. `68/214/241 (remote has no final newline; wc -l prints 240)`.

problem: Any non-zero `git merge` exit, including a fatal error (exit 128), is treated as the expected conflict, and the script prints 'is mid-merge' even when the index has no unmerged entries.
fix: After the failed merge, add `[ -n "$(g ls-files -u)" ] || die "merge failed without leaving a conflict"` before the success echo.

problem: The project map still lists cases as `base.txt local.txt remote.txt expected.json (planned)`. That contradicts the layout now committed (`<ext>` files plus README.md) and docs/architecture.md:63, so readers have two versions of the same fact (vision 2).
fix: The orchestrator updates the line to `tests/golden/<case>  base.<ext> local.<ext> remote.<ext> README.md, expected.json (generated); scripts/golden-repo.sh` (agents may not edit skills or docs, DR5).

problem: The one-letter helper name `g` makes the owner trace back to the definition at every call site to see that it is git run inside the case repo with the isolated identity.

problem: The open risk names git ≥ 2.28 as the floor, but `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` [INFERENCE] needs git ≥ 2.32. On older git (e.g. stock macOS before Xcode 13) it is ignored without warning, so the user's global config (such as merge.conflictStyle) leaks into the rebuilt repo.

problem: The test is still named `enough_generated_triples_are_clean_for_both_to_exercise_the_cross_check`, but it now also asserts the RK13 dangerous-direction ceiling (line 229). A reader of a failing `only_git_conflicts` assertion gets a name that describes a different behaviour; the implementer listed this as an open risk.

problem: CM1 mapped `to` with +1 while claiming chunks never swallow adjacent insertions; with line ranges that end at the start of the next line, +1 swallows typing on the next line, and an end-of-last-line representation cannot tell a one-empty-line chunk from an insertion point.

problem: tone.ts exports four things (Tone, Side, CHANGED_SIDES, chunkTone), and the centre pane's 'BothSame → local' rule is hidden in the position of the first element (`CHANGED_SIDES[kind][0]` at chunkField.ts:45), which a reader cannot see from either file.

problem: `lineStart(doc, line: number)` takes an engine line as a bare number, which is the exact TS1 violation shape, and the from/to pair `lineStart(doc, r.start)` / `lineStart(doc, r.start + r.len)` is written twice (chunkField.ts:46-47, decorations.ts:39-40).
fix: Replace it with `lineSpan(doc: Text, range: Chunk["base"] | Chunk["local"] | Chunk["remote"]): { from: number; to: number }` (rename the file to match) and spread it at both call sites.

problem: `const spans` holds a StateField, not spans, and the new `chunks:` property (lines 26, 33, 40; pane.ts:95) holds an Extension, while two lines above `chunks` is the destructured `Chunk[]`. The same name means two things in one expression: `chunks: sideDecorations(chunks, "local")`.
fix: Rename the local to `chunkSpans` (or `field`, as the tests already call it) and rename createPane's parameter to `decorations`.

problem: Correctness depends on the last `restoreSpans` effect winning, because history concatenates the older event's inverted effects last when it merges steps. Nothing in the code says so, so a maintainer could 'simplify' the loop to the first match and silently break undo of merged typing.
fix: Write it as `const restored = tr.effects.findLast((e) => e.is(restoreSpans));` with a one-line CP1 comment: `// history merges events with the oldest inverted effects last — @codemirror/commands HistoryState.addChanges`.

problem: After this patch the docs describe a different design: the state table here and in docs/architecture.md:358 says positions are only 'remapped via tr.changes.mapPos' (they are now also restored by an inverted effect on undo); VU14 (vue-conventions/SKILL.md:50) says theme.css uses `@apply`; and CM1 still prescribes `+1` for `to`. The implementer's report lists only CM1 and the MergeTexts mentions.
fix: Orchestrator: update the state-table row in project-map:70 and architecture.md:358 to 'mapped with mapPos(-1) both ends; restored on undo via a restoreSpans invertedEffect', change VU14's `@apply` to `var(--color-*)` (matching architecture.md:493), and rewrite CM1 to the brief's start-of-next-line representation.

problem: The class names `chunk-gap-above` / `chunk-gap-below` reuse 'gap', which the project already uses for merge-core's `Options::gap` and for the alignment rows rejected in plan row 11.
fix: Rename them to `chunk-point-above` / `chunk-point-below` in decorations.ts, theme.css and decorations.test.ts.

problem: At an unterminated end of file a chunk's `to` is doc.length, the end of its last line, not the start of a next line. With -1, text typed at the end of that line, or Enter plus a new line, lands outside the chunk. This contradicts the brief's 'typing anywhere in the chunk's lines stays inside' and differs from the terminated case, where the new line joins the band.
fix: For a non-empty span whose `to` is not a line start in `tr.startState.doc`, map `to` with +1 (keep -1 for line-start `to` and for empty spans). Add a test: 'a\nb' with {1,1}, insert '\nc' at 3 ⇒ [2,5).

problem: All four tone classes write one shared `--chunk-tone` per line. When a center edit puts an empty chunk's marker on another chunk's band line (e.g. the user deletes the lines between them), the whole line takes whichever tone comes later in this file: an empty Conflict marker turns a modified band line red. A line with both gap-above and gap-below loses one shadow.
fix: Emit the marker's tone as its own class (e.g. `chunk-gap-above gap-${tone}` setting `--chunk-gap-tone`) and read that in the box-shadow rules, with a `.chunk-gap-above.chunk-gap-below` rule that draws both shadows.

problem: The undo test covers a single history event only. The 'last restoreSpans wins' rule (chunkField.ts:51-55) is what makes undo of a merged typing group restore the group's start ranges, and it would survive being changed to 'first wins'. Redo is never exercised.
fix: Add a case: delete [5,13), then insert 'x' at 5 (merged into the same history event), undo once ⇒ doc MAPPED_BASE and ranges [[5,13],[19,19]]; then redo ⇒ [[5,5],[11,11]] with the deletion and 'x' re-applied.

problem: No test checks which side gives the center its tone. Replacing `CHANGED_SIDES[chunk.kind][0]` with `"local"` passes every test, because the fixtures used have no LocalOnly/RemoteOnly deletion, and for inserted or modified the unchanged side gives the same tone. The `chunk-deleted` class is never asserted in any pane.
fix: In decorations.test.ts, add a synthetic RemoteOnly deletion (base len 2, local len 2, remote len 0) asserting center `chunk-deleted chunk-band` on both lines, right `chunk-deleted chunk-gap-above` at the point, and nothing on the left.

problem: The const `IN_HOSTILE_ENVIRONMENT` holds the libtest path of the child test `tests::ordinary_conflict_in_the_inherited_environment`, but its name reads like a setting or a flag, not like the test name it contains.

problem: The expected stderr hard-codes the libc text `Is a directory (os error 21)`, so the test pins the platform's error string instead of yamt's message format; this is the implementer's own macOS open risk (macOS is planned for M3).

problem: The hostile test only sets `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, so deleting `.env_remove("GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS")` (lib.rs:56) still passes every test. Half of the contract's env isolation has no detector, and cargo-mutants cannot remove a chained call.

problem: The new +1 for a mid-line `to` lets spans overlap, and an overlap crashes the center editor. Repro from the joined state of decorations.test.ts:134 (Conflict [0,1), point [1,1], doc 'ab\n'): insert '\n  x' at 1, as a paste or Enter with auto-indent does. The Conflict becomes [0,5) while the point stays at 1. bandDecorations then adds line 2 (from 2) before the point's line 1 (from 0), so RangeSetBuilder throws 'Ranges must be added sorted', `state.update` throws, and the edit is rejected. Round 1's -1/-1 mapping was monotone and could not overlap.
fix: In mapSpans, cap each mapped `to` at the next span's mapped `from` (spans are sorted). Add a test: from that joined state, insert '\n  x' at 1 ⇒ ranges [[0,1],[1,1]] and runsOf does not throw.

problem: No test types at an empty span that sits mid-line, so the `span.from < span.to` guard in endsMidLine (chunkField.ts:30) can be deleted with every test still passing. The 'lands after it' test uses point 19, which is a line start and maps with -1 anyway. Without the guard, a point at an unterminated end of file would swallow the text typed there.
fix: Add a case: 'a\nb' with chunk {2,0} (the point 3 = doc.length), insert 'c' at 3 ⇒ ranges [[3,3]].

problem: The merged-undo test relies on both `state.update` calls landing within history's 500 ms newGroupDelay of Date.now(), so a stalled runner splits the event and the undo assertion fails (the implementer's own open risk).
fix: Give both edits the same `annotations: Transaction.time.of(0)` in the test's `edit` helper, so the history grouping is deterministic.

problem: After rework item 5 these docs no longer match the code: CM1 says 'both map with tr.changes.mapPos(pos, -1)', and so do the state tables at project-map/SKILL.md:70 and docs/architecture.md:358. The code now maps a non-empty span's `to` with +1 when it is not a line start (chunkField.ts:29-31, 41).
fix: Orchestrator: change the three places to 'from maps -1; to maps -1 when it is a line start or the span is empty, +1 when a non-empty span ends mid-line (unterminated last line, or after a join)'.

problem: The pane union `"local" | "center" | "remote"` is spelled out twice (lines 5 and 12), and the side union `"local" | "remote"` a third time as `sideOf`'s return type next to decorations.ts:10.

problem: just mutants: 9 survivors in fixture.ts and 1 in store.ts:22 are equivalent or unobservable — Record<K,true> values unused (membership via Object.hasOwn), typeof guard redundant with hasOwn, Error cause not user-visible, ticket += vs -= both unique; useMergeController.ts has no coverage by design (architecture §8: wiring not tested; covered by WebKit smoke).

problem: tone.ts again exports four names (Tone, Side, sideChanged, chunkTone). That undoes rework 1.1 item 1, which cut tone.ts to Tone + chunkTone (TS11) and moved Side/CHANGED_SIDES out. The same slice also adds geometry.ts with five exports and scrollSync.ts with four, so TS11 has been exceeded in three consecutive slices (0.0 log.ts, 1.1 tone.ts, 1.2).

problem: `Pane` now means two different unions in sibling files: tone.ts:5 `"local" | "center" | "remote"` and geometry.ts:9 `"left" | "center" | "right"`. strips.ts:16-17 has to translate one into the other (`side === "local" ? row.left : row.center`), so a reader has to check which `Pane` each signature means.

problem: chunkRows zips two parallel arrays by index: MergeController's `#chunks` and the field's spans. A runtime throw guards the 'one span per chunk, in order' invariant, inside the rAF, where it would silently stop all later painting and syncing. The implementer listed this invariant as an open risk.
fix: Have ChunkSpan carry `chunk: Chunk` (in place of `id`/`kind`, set once in chunkField's create; mapSpans' spread keeps it). Then chunkRows(views, centerSpans) maps one array, and `#chunks`, the index lookup and the throw all go away.

problem: After this patch the dependency diagram is wrong. Line 56 (and architecture.md §2 lines 88-90) shows `model ◄── connectors ◄── ui`, but the only importer of connectors is editor/ (strips.ts, geometry.ts, scrollSync.ts), ui/ never imports it, and connectors imports nothing from model (line 33 also says model is shared with connectors).
fix: The orchestrator (owner of docs/.omp) changes line 56 to `connectors ◄── editor` and the architecture §2 mermaid from `ui --> connectors` to `editor --> connectors`, and drops connectors from model's line 33.

problem: The name `#syncing` (with `#release` beside it) reads like the boolean flag in CM12, but it holds the follower panes whose next scroll event is an echo of our own write.
fix: Rename it to `#echoes` and `#release` to `#clearEchoes`, so the per-pane deviation from CM12's single flag is visible in the names.

problem: sync() re-maps from any scroll event on a pane even when its scrollTop did not change: a horizontal scroll (lines do not wrap, so horizontal scrolling is common), a CM horizontal scrollIntoView, or an echo that arrives late (open risk 1). If a follower is being held at an insertion point (e.g. the user scrolled remote 98-106 in vueuse), such an event snaps the user's pane to the chunk's top or bottom. The report calls this a harmless jitter, but here it is a visible jump. The feedback-loop check ran at a spot where a mis-attributed echo writes back identical values, so that check could not have seen it.
fix: Keep the vertical scrollTop of every pane as it was after the last sync, reading it back inside the rAF right after the writes. At the start of sync(), return early when `views[source].scrollDOM.scrollTop` still equals the recorded value. Then repeat the feedback-loop check with the right pane scrolled into the middle of vueuse remote 98-106.

problem: Every scrollSync test builds `ends` with the same offset per pane as the last chunk bottom, e.g. 5/12: (10,17,17) vs (20,27,27); beyond: (5,3,8) vs (40,38,43). So deleting the content-end anchor from anchorsOf (scrollSync.ts:21) leaves every test green, even though the brief names it as an anchor.
fix: Add a case where the tails differ, e.g. a chunk bottom at (10,17,17) with ends(20,27,30). Assert that `targets(anchors, "center", 27 * LINE_PX).right === 30 * LINE_PX` and that a point midway between the chunk bottom and the end interpolates.

problem: The project map is stale after this rework. Line 34's editor internal/ list omits the new `side`. Line 33 still says model/ is 'shared by editor/ and connectors/', while line 56 says 'model/ is empty and unused'.
fix: The orchestrator adds `side` to line 34's internal/ list and changes line 33 to 'empty, unused; planned for pure TS shared by more than one module'.

problem: The side mirror field sets its own initial status (`status: "pending"` in create) independently of chunkField's create, so two places define the initial chunk status and the mirror is a second source of truth for that fact until the first showStatuses push.
fix: Make sideStatusField take `readonly ChunkState[]`. In MergeController.#createViews, create the center pane first and seed both side panes with `sideStatusField(center.state.field(field))`, so the mirror never sets a status of its own. Adjust decorations.test.ts's sideBands helper the same way.

problem: applyChunk, applyAllNonConflicting (line 59) and dismissChunk (line 80) only build and return a TransactionSpec, yet they are named as actions. applyAllNonConflicting shares its name with the MergeController method that dispatches it (index.ts:133-134), so a reader of index.ts sees a method calling a same-named function with different semantics.
fix: Name the builders for what they return, e.g. `applySpec`, `bulkApplySpec`, `dismissSpec`, and update the index.ts and apply.test.ts call sites.

problem: #act branches on ChunkAction.kind with a ternary, so a third ChunkAction variant would silently fall into dismissChunk instead of failing to compile.
fix: Use a `switch (action.kind)` with `case "apply"`, `case "dismiss"` and the `default: { const _exhaustive: never = action; … }` arm.

problem: paintStrips repeats an almost identical 15-line block for the left and right strip, differing only in strip, pane pair and side. The old code had a single paintGap helper for this, so each future change to strip painting has to be made twice.
fix: Restore one `paintGap(strip, panes: { left, right }, arrowView, side, rows, onAction)` that measures stripTop and calls replaceChildren(bandPaths…, arrowGroups…), and call it twice from paintStrips.

problem: status.ts exports seven items (ChunkStatus, ChunkState, MergeSummary, isResolved, canApply, statusAfterApply, summarize), as do apply.ts (5) and strips.ts (3). This breaks TS11's 'one exported thing per file', which pre-existing geometry.ts also ignores, so the rule and the code disagree.
fix: Keep status.ts as one cohesive status module, and have the curator reword TS11 to 'one concept per file (a type, its constructors and predicates)' so the rule matches the code instead of forcing a split into many tiny files.

problem: The composable restates `"local" | "remote"` because MergeController.applyAllNonConflicting's public signature uses the internal Side type, which editor/index.ts does not export.
fix: Add `export type { Side } from "./internal/side"` to editor/index.ts and type the composable parameter as `Side` (re-exported next to MergeSummary).

problem: `latestOpen` now also tickets reset(), so the name no longer matches what it counts.
fix: Rename it to `latestLoad` (it tickets every load that replaces `data`).

problem: The only CRLF test builds its states with eolSeparator directly and checks state.sliceDoc(); it never goes through createPane or resultText(). It stays green if `eolSeparator(pane.eol)` is dropped from createPane or resultText() switches to doc.toString(), and the smoke file is LF, so nothing catches CRLF files being sent to finishFile as LF (brief Tests line 'resultText() of a CRLF file contains \r\n', CM5).
fix: Move createPane's EditorState construction into an exported pane.ts function (e.g. `paneState({ kind, doc, eol, language, extensions })`, which createPane then mounts), build the test's center and side states with it, and assert `\r\n` in the text the controller serialises. Alternatively, add a WebKit browser test that calls MergeController.resultText() on a CRLF record.

problem: If the user deletes the unchanged line between a half-applied conflict C and the next chunk D, the « apply inserts at C.to == D.from. D.from maps with -1 to before the insertion, and the clamp cuts C.to back to D.from. The appended remote lines then belong to D (coloured as D), and applying D later silently replaces them. The same happens when applying an empty-range insertion chunk that has become adjacent to the next chunk.
fix: In mapSpans, when `span` is in `applied` and overruns `next.from`, raise `next.from` (and `next.to` if it is lower) to `span.to` instead of clamping `span.to`. Add a test: delete the separator line, apply » then «, assert centerText(C) === local + remote and that D's range starts after it.

problem: Arrows act on `click`, so a repaint between press and release replaces the <g> and the click is lost (the implementer's open risk). [INFERENCE] The mousedown on the non-focusable strip also blurs the center editor, so Ctrl+Z right after clicking » does nothing until the user clicks back into the middle pane; the smoke only used toolbar Undo.
fix: Dispatch the action on `pointerdown` on the group, and add one `mousedown` listener on each strip <svg> that calls `preventDefault()` so the center keeps focus. Add one smoke step that presses Ctrl+Z after an arrow click.

problem: The 'N changes · M conflict(s)' / 'All changes processed' label (a Behaviour line) has untested branches: zero is omitted, singular vs plural, and the all-done text. ui/ is inside the mutation run, so mutants of `counted` and `remaining` will survive, and the smoke never reached 'All changes processed'.
fix: Move the label logic into a pure exported function in a ui/ .ts module (e.g. `summaryLabel(summary)`) and add a node test for {0,0}, {1,0}, {0,1}, {3,1} and {2,2}.

problem: #createViews now spans lines 81–128, 48 lines, over TS11's 40-line function limit. It was at the limit before; the multi-line destructured object signature (8 lines) pushed it over, and no lint checks function length.
fix: Declare `type ViewSources = { data: FileMergeData; hosts: MergeHosts; language: LanguageSupport | null }` next to MergeHosts. Write the signature on one line as `#createViews({ data, hosts, language }: ViewSources): PaneViews {`, and fold `const { eol } = data;` into `const shared = { eol: data.eol, language };`.

problem: `#colour` loads a grammar, logs on failure and reconfigures the language compartment, but its name says only 'colour'. A reader looking for where grammars load won't find it by name.
fix: Rename `#colour` to `#loadLanguage`.

problem: The compartment receives the whole LanguageSupport, which brings editing behaviours into the editable center pane, not just colours. lang-html, lang-vue and JSX bring autoCloseTags (typing '>' inserts '</tag>'). lang-markdown brings a Prec.high Enter/Backspace keymap that continues list markup, plus pasteURLAsLink. These change the result text the user types in a merge, and the brief asked for syntax colours only.
fix: Put only the parsing language in the compartment: `support.language` (a `Language`) in #colour and `description.support?.language` in the constructor, typing paneState's `language` as `Language | null`. Nested grammars (Vue's TS script, HTML style/script, Markdown code blocks) are configured inside that Language's parser, so colours stay the same and the pane.test assertions still prove it. If the extras are wanted, the orchestrator should ratify them in plan §2 #29 instead.

problem: Lezer uses `tags.character` for character literals (@lezer/java CharacterLiteral, @lezer/rust Char, @lezer/go Rune, @lezer/cpp CharLiteral), so the brief-mandated `character` → link rule draws 'a' in link blue in Java/Rust/Go/C/C++. Without that rule they would inherit the string green, as WebStorm draws them. The `angleBracket` → tag rule (line 69) likewise paints C++ template brackets gold, because @lezer/cpp tags '< >' as angleBracket.
fix: Have the orchestrator amend the brief: drop `tags.character` from the link rule (HTML and Markdown entities then fall back to the string colour) or accept the cross-language effect explicitly. Then pin the chosen behaviour with one pane.test case, e.g. a Rust `'a'` literal.

problem: The test is named '…its script setup as TypeScript', but it would still pass if the script were parsed as plain JavaScript (for example if the lang="ts" nesting were lost), because `const` and "hi" are keyword and string in both dialects. Nothing proves the TypeScript claim in the brief's Behaviour list.

problem: The rework decision says typing in the middle pane 'behaves as before', but a loaded `Language` still changes Enter. defaultKeymap's insertNewlineAndIndent now indents from the grammar's syntax tree in Vue/HTML/Python/etc. Before this slice, those files had no language, so Enter just copied the previous line's indentation. TypeScript is unchanged, because it always had a grammar.

problem: just mutants 36272da: all survivors sit on lines this slice did not change. cargo: decode.rs:6 MAX_TEXT_BYTES `8 * 1024 * 1024` `*`→`+` (×2), pulled into the diff hunk by the removed import; the tests are written relative to the constant on purpose → equivalent. Stryker fixture.ts: 18–24 Record values `true`→`false` in CHUNK_KINDS/EOLS (membership is by key) and 28:16 `typeof input === "string"`→`true` (non-string keys miss anyway) → equivalent; 63:99 `{ cause: error }`→`{}` → the parse error cause is not asserted.
fix: Ride-along for the next slice touching fixture.ts: assert the thrown error keeps the valibot cause.

problem: Owner: on a conflict it is hard to see what exactly changed compared to base; WebStorm uses a brighter tint of red for the parts of the conflicting change that differ from base, so left and right are easy to compare. Today it is one red block per side; in bigger blocks the eye cannot find the change.
fix: Plan §2 #30: word-level changes computed in merge-core, drawn as brighter marks on all three panes (conflict and modified blocks, WebStorm parity). Slices 1.D (engine + contract) then 1.E (editor).

problem: `is_highlighted` looks up again (`tokens.get(index) else false`) the token its only caller already holds. `is_changed_text` takes an `Option<usize>` and falls back on `changed.get(index).unwrap_or(false)` for a vector that always has the same length as `tokens`. Some of these branches can never run, such as `checked_add(1)` returning None or `get` missing. A beginner reader must work out that the two vectors run in parallel, and why each fallback exists.
fix: In `ranges`, first build one `text_changed: Vec<bool>` (changed and not a line break). Then pass `token.kind`, `text_changed[index]` and the two neighbours to `is_highlighted`, reading them as `index.checked_sub(1).and_then(|before| text_changed.get(before))` and `text_changed.get(index + 1)`. Delete the `Option<usize>` parameter and the `tokens.get` fallback.

problem: `kind_of` never returns `TokenKind::LineBreak`, yet the tokenizer's `byte_len` match must still handle it as `Symbol | LineBreak`. This is a branch that can never run, and it exists only because one enum describes both a character's kind and a token's kind.
fix: Have `kind_of` return a three-variant enum (`Word | Space | Symbol`) used only while splitting a line, and add `LineBreak` only to `TokenKind`, so the `byte_len` match lists only reachable arms.

problem: The 'sorted' assertion `line < next_line || start + len < next_start` accepts a later range on an earlier line whenever its column is larger. For example (5,0,1),(2,3,1) passes, so a union built by concatenating the two sides' base ranges without sorting would survive the proptest.
fix: Assert `line < next_line || (line == next_line && start + len < next_start)`.

problem: No test covers the `token.kind != TokenKind::LineBreak` guard in is_changed_text. A mutant that drops it, so that a whitespace run between a changed word and a changed line break gets highlighted, passes every hand test and proptest; the proptests never check over-highlighting.
fix: Add a hand test such as base `x old \n`, local `x new \r\n` expecting local [(0,2,3)] and base [(0,2,3)]. The trailing space must stay unhighlighted even though both of its neighbours changed.

problem: The acceptance eyeball output shows the LocalOnly/RemoteOnly chunks 5 and 6 of vueuse-use-magic-keys, but the brief asks for a modified chunk of another golden. The by-eye check therefore covers only one file's style; for example, nuxt-island-test's large re-indented conflict is not shown.
fix: Rerun the throwaway printer on one LocalOnly or RemoteOnly chunk of a different golden (e.g. nuxt-island-test or vue-core-playground-app) and paste the output into the report.

problem: Eyeball of nuxt-island-test chunk 0 (local): the token diff runs over the whole chunk, so histogram matches base `/utils'` on line 2 to the new line 3. Local line 2 (identical to base line 2) gets `[utils']`, base line 2 gets `[-vitest]`, and the added line 3 is only partly marked. Unchanged lines get marks; an added line looks half-changed.
fix: Line-anchored word diff (IntelliJ: by line, then by word inside changed lines): diff the chunk's lines first; run the token diff only inside each changed line hunk; lines equal to their aligned base line get no marks.

problem: In `token_span(&self, lines: &Range<u32>)`, `lines` is a range of line indices relative to the chunk, while the struct's own `lines` field holds line text and `Token.line` is absolute. The reader must infer from the `first_line +` addition which line space the parameter is in.
fix: ride-along for the next slice touching word.rs: Rename the parameter to `hunk_lines` (and, if it still reads ambiguously, the method to `tokens_of_hunk_lines`), so the chunk-relative space is named at the signature.

problem: The early `fill(true)` return in mark_changed_tokens gives the same result as the general path, because imara-diff marks every token of the non-empty side when the other side is empty. Its `||`→`&&` mutant therefore survives `just mutants` by construction.
fix: ride-along for the next slice touching word.rs: Delete the early return and let the token diff mark one-sided hunks. Alternatively, keep it and name the surviving mutant in open_risks next to the `unwrap_or_default` survivors.

problem: The rule 'a pane shows a block's word marks exactly when it shows its tint' exists as two independent copies. One is the side gate `!sideChanged(chunk, side) || isResolved(chunk, status)` at words.ts:18, mirroring decorations.ts:41; the other is the centre `isResolved` gate at words.ts:33, mirroring decorations.ts:53. A future change to the tint gate would silently leave the word marks on the old rule, which breaks vision 2 (one source of truth per fact).
fix: Fold sideMarks/centerMarks into decorations.ts so that each pane's single `EditorView.decorations.compute` filters chunks once and emits both bands and word marks. Alternatively, extract one predicate, e.g. `showsTint(state, pane)` in status.ts, and call it from all four sites.

problem: Two docs are stale after this slice. The editor internals list (architecture.md:395-407) and the project-map tree (`editor/internal/: pane, chunkField, decorations, …`) do not mention words.ts. The state-ownership table also does not record that the centre pane keeps its initial base Text in `originalDoc`. A reader looking for where word marks are drawn, or what owns the base text used by the middle gate, cannot find it in the docs.

problem: Two names are used for the same value. The field is called `originalDoc`, while its only reader, `centerMarks(doc, base, …)` at words.ts:30, calls it `base`.

problem: Every middle-pane 'text changed' case changes the block's length: ' // x' is inserted, and 'mine' (4 chars) replaces 'old' (3). So a gate that only compares `span.to - span.from` with the original length (losing the sliceString compare at words.ts:39) passes all five tests, while marks would stay on a same-length edit such as replacing 'old' with 'new'.

problem: The 0.65-alpha word mark is painted above CodeMirror's selection layer (drawSelection draws it behind the content at z-index -1 and makes native ::selection transparent), so a selection inside a word mark changes the background by only about (1,7,20) RGB. Selected text in the marked words, which is exactly what a user copies from a side pane (CM3 keeps selection and copy), is effectively invisible. The implementer raised this risk and never checked it.
fix: Screenshot a selection across a word mark in a side pane; if it cannot be told apart, make the selection paint over the marks (e.g. `.cm-editor .cm-selectionLayer { z-index: 1 }` with reduced layer opacity in theme.css), and add the screenshot to the evidence.

problem: The report says the gate is 'O(1) per chunk when the lengths differ'. But a keystroke outside every block leaves every span's length unchanged, so each keystroke allocates and compares the full text of every open chunk that has base words: the usual case, not the worst case.
fix: Correct the cost statement in the report (or skip the compare for spans the transaction did not touch, via `tr.changes.touchesRange`, if a later slice needs it).

problem: The selection colour is now set by two separate rules in `darkTheme`: the long `.cm-selectionBackground, … ::selection` selector at pane.ts:37-38 and a new `.selected-text` rule at pane.ts:40. A reader changing how selection looks can miss one of them.

problem: just mutants b25f7f5 (cargo): missed 123:12 delete `!` in tokens (line-break tokens dropped / empty ones added). No test has a trailing space between a changed word on one line and a changed word on the next line of the same hunk, where the line-break token is what stops the whitespace bridge. Other misses equivalent: 65:62 `<`→`<=` in token_span (adds an equal line to both sides; reviewer), 190:24 `||`→`&&` in mark_changed_tokens (same result by construction; #191); timeout 107:48 counts as caught. Stryker fixture.ts survivors are the Record-value/typeof equivalents of #182.

Ride-along for the next slice touching word.rs: hand test base `a x 
b y
`, local `a X 
B y

problem: Smoke 1.D/1.E (d): after applying a change with an arrow, Ctrl+Z in the middle pane and the toolbar Undo both restore the text but jump the view to the top of the file (line 1), so the user loses the block they were working on. [INFERENCE] history restores the selection from before the apply transaction, which stays at its old position (often 0) because arrow clicks do not move the cursor, and undo scrolls it into view. Present since 1.4 (not noticed in the wave-4 smoke).

problem: Owner (language-tools-script-setup chunk 3): conflict word marks are 'still chaotic and unhelpful'. Owner expects: left = local vs base, right = remote vs base. Observed causes: (1) middle pane marks the union of both sides' base changes in one tone, so ~all base text is marked with no side attribution; (2) local's only edit is a dedent + removed wrapper, so left marks are leading-whitespace runs only; (3) token diff runs over the whole multi-line hunk, so whitespace/word tokens pair across lines (local 370 `yield ${macro}` fully marked although unchanged, sibling `}` lines inconsistent).
fix: Pending owner decision after explanation: candidates are ignore indentation-only changes, drop or attribute middle-pane union marks, pair tokens per line within a hunk.

problem: Owner rejected the orchestrator's suggestion to hide indentation-only changes: indentation still counts as a change. The real defect is marks on text that did not change (local line 370 fully marked, sibling re-indented lines unmarked).

problem: `StateField` is still imported as a value but only used in type positions now; elsewhere the repo imports it as `type StateField`.
