problem: paintGap rebuilds both strips from new nodes (paths, groups, titles, rects, imported icon svgs, one pointerdown listener per icon) and replaceChildren on every scroll frame. pnpm-lock.yaml with inactive views skipped: 34.9 ms mean; strips built but never inserted: 20.3; strips hidden: 17.3. contain:strict on strips/panes did not help.
fix: Keep strip nodes; update positions per frame; create/remove only when a band/icon enters/leaves or status/covered changes.

problem: chunkRows (3 lineBlockAt per chunk) and the scroll sync's anchorsOf run over every chunk on every scroll frame: ~4 ms per frame on pnpm-lock.yaml's 186 chunks (controller JS with strips hidden), though chunk heights change only with doc, measured heights or find space.
fix: Recompute rows/anchors on doc/geometry/status/find-space change; reuse them per scroll frame.

problem: geometry.ts was a single vocabulary (where each chunk sits in each pane, in document px), but now also holds what each strip shows: crossesStrip, gapArrows (apply mode and open sides), bandPaints (strip-space SVG paths with tones), Arrow and BandPaint. These were moved only so strips.ts fits under 300 lines; the stated PM6 reason does not hold, because the orchestrator applies the implementer's other doc edits outside its globs.
fix: Move crossesStrip, gapArrows, bandPaints, Arrow and BandPaint into a new editor/internal module (e.g. gap.ts, 'what a strip shows'), update the imports in strips.ts, drag.ts and the tests, and list the file in the project-map Tree among the editor internals (orchestrator).

problem: `Arrow.top` means two different things: gapArrows returns document-relative tops (drag.ts:41 relies on that), while GapStrip.measure re-emits the same `Arrow` type with strip-relative tops in GapPaint.arrows. A reader cannot tell from the type which coordinate space a given Arrow is in.
fix: Keep `Arrow` in document space and give placed rows their own field, e.g. `GapPaint.arrows: readonly { readonly arrow: Arrow; readonly y: number }[]`, with `y` used for the transform and the crossesStrip filter.

problem: The #anchors memo is keyed on the identity of rows but also captures ends(views) (three lineBlockAt calls). It is correct only because the controller happens to drop #rowsCache on every geometryChanged (index.ts:107), so the answer to 'what can change the anchors?' lives in another file, and two derived-geometry caches have to stay in step.
fix: Have the controller's one cache hold both rows and anchorsOf(rows, ends(views)), dropped by rowsChanged, and pass the anchors into ScrollSync.sync; then delete #anchors and #anchorsOf.

problem: The comment cites '(slice 3.P)' as the source of the 5 ms/frame WebKitGTK 2.54 measurement, but docs/slices/briefs/3.P-scroll-performance.md does not contain that measurement; it exists only in .omp/run/notes/V0ScrollSmooth.md. That leaves a WebKit-specific compositing decision (will-change-transform wrappers) without a durable reference or a plan §2 row (DR2), as the implementer's own open risk says.

problem: The proposed replacement for architecture.md:464, '(buttons persist; positions updated per frame)', is wrong: a button row is removed when it leaves the strip, when its side closes, or when its look changes (strips.ts:233-245). That is exactly why pointer capture must stay on the persistent <svg>, and 'buttons persist' suggests capture on a button would work.

problem: The list of stale docs misses three statements the patch makes false: architecture.md:404 ('connector geometry | computed per frame from lineBlockAt, never stored'); architecture.md:496 and the project-map ui row ('inactive ones `invisible`' / 'inactive = `invisible`'), since inactive views are now also content-visibility:hidden. The proposed project-map state row also omits the ScrollSync anchors memo.

problem: `look` is a space-joined string of mode, applyX, ignoreX and lineHeight used as an equality key; the name does not say it decides whether a row is rebuilt.
fix: Store `mode` and `buttons` on ArrowRow and compare them in a small `sameShape(row, mode, buttons)` predicate, or at least rename the field to `shapeKey`.

problem: The read-only case is checked twice: measure returns no arrows when #onPress is null (line 192), and paint checks #onPress again only to narrow its type for #paintArrows.
fix: Check once: have paint pass `this.#onPress` into #paintArrows unconditionally, typed `OnPress | null` and only reached when there are arrows, or drop the check in measure and keep the one in paint.

problem: `bandPaints` is a new pure exported helper but has no test, against the brief's rule that new pure helpers get boundary tests. It holds the side selection (local→left/center, remote→center/right), the per-side shift and the min-top/max-bottom visibility test. Swapping `shifts.left`/`shifts.right`, or testing only `onLeft`, would pass all 333 tests, and the smoke compared only bands near the middle.
fix: Add geometry.test.ts cases on a fixture's rows: local vs remote pick the right span pair with their own shift (compare `d` to `bandPath` of the expected band), a band whose left edge is above the strip while its right edge is inside is kept, and a band 1 px outside is dropped.

problem: The anchors memo is valid only if the caller hands over a new rows array whenever any pane's geometry changes. That contract is enforced in index.ts:107-109, a different module, and stated nowhere in ScrollSync, so a future caller that reuses or mutates a rows array gets stale anchors and misaligned panes without a type error.
fix: Keep one cache: have the controller cache `{ rows, anchors }` together (anchors from `anchorsOf(rows, ends)` filled lazily on the same invalidation) and pass anchors to `sync`. Alternatively, name the 'new array ⇔ geometry changed' contract on `sync`'s parameter.

problem: The implementer's list of doc edits omits two statements this patch makes wrong: architecture.md:496 'inactive ones `invisible`' and project-map SKILL.md:52 '(inactive = `invisible`)'. Both now describe only half of the hiding and imply inactive views are still laid out, which is the cause this slice removes.
fix: Add both to the orchestrator's doc edits, e.g. 'inactive ones `invisible [content-visibility:hidden]` (skips layout and paint, keeps scrollTop; `invisible` stops the root's box from taking hit tests)'.

problem: `#rowsCache`/`#rows()` hand out a mutable `ChunkRow[]` that is now shared across frames, `released` and ScrollSync's memo, so any caller's push/sort would silently corrupt every later frame.
fix: Type the cache and `#rows()` as `readonly ChunkRow[]` (all consumers already accept readonly arrays).

problem: Three of the proposed doc sentences say gap.ts picks 'bands and icons that cross each strip' or 'icons in view': (a) 'gap (what a strip shows: bands and icons in view)', (d) 'gap.ts (what a strip shows: bands and icons that cross it)' and (f) 'gap.ts picks the bands and icons that cross each strip'. In the code, gapArrows (gap.ts:15-23) returns every open chunk's icon row in document space, and the strip filter for icons runs in GapStrip.measure (strips.ts:205-207). Sentence (f) also attaches 'cached until rowsChanged' to geometry.ts, but the cache lives in MergeController (index.ts:215-221).
fix: Reword before the orchestrator writes them. (a)/(d): 'gap (what a strip shows: the bands that cross it and each open change's icon row, document space)'. (f): 'gap.ts picks the bands that cross each strip and the open changes' icon rows; strips.ts places the rows, keeps those in view and moves their kept nodes once per frame', with the 'cached until rowsChanged' clause attached to MergeController.

problem: crossesStrip(top, bottom, height) takes three swappable numbers positionally. It is now in gap.ts, which is not in TS7's list of per-frame paths (connectors/, scrollSync.ts, strips.ts) that may do this, although it runs every frame like strips.ts.
fix: Add gap.ts to TS7's per-frame list in skill://ts-conventions (orchestrator/curator), so the rule matches the file the code moved to.

problem: The proposed doc sentences (a), (d) and (f) say gap.ts picks the 'bands and icons that cross each strip' / 'icons in view'. In fact gapArrows (gap.ts:15-23) returns every open icon in document space (drag.ts depends on that), and the icon crossing filter lives in strips.ts GapStrip.measure (strips.ts:206-208). The docs would therefore send a reader to the wrong file.
fix: Have the orchestrator write that gap.ts gives the bands that cross a strip and every open icon's document-space top, and that strips.ts places the icons in strip space and keeps the ones that cross it. Apply the same wording in (a), (d) and (f).

problem: Every fixture row is PENDING and the tested chunk is a Conflict, which has the same tone on both sides. Two mutants therefore survive all of gap.test.ts: removing the `isSideOpen` guard in bandPaints (gap.ts:32), which would keep drawing a band after its side is applied or ignored, and computing `chunkTone` for the wrong side (gap.ts:40).

problem: The brief asked for hand mutations of gap.ts while owning only gap.test.ts; the ownership hook blocked the edit and the implementer proved the mutants with temporary vi.mock stand-ins instead.

problem: The type parameter is written as `ChunkStatus["local"]`, but status.ts already exports this union as `SideStatus` and sides.test.ts:15 imports it under that name, so the same type now goes by two names.
fix: Import `type SideStatus` from `./status` and write `test.each<SideStatus>(["applied", "ignored"])`.

problem: The two assertions in the tone test repeat the same `bandPaints(...).map(({ chunk, tone }) => [chunk.id, tone])` call. The formatter wraps the two copies differently, so they look less alike than they are.
fix: Add a local `function tonesOn(side: Side)` that returns the `[id, tone]` pairs, then assert `expect(tonesOn("local")).toEqual([[0, "deleted"]])` and `expect(tonesOn("remote")).toEqual([[1, "deleted"]])`.

problem: `test.each<ChunkStatus["local"]>` spells the per-side status as an indexed access type, while status.ts exports it by name as `SideStatus`.
fix: Import `type SideStatus` from "./status" and write `test.each<SideStatus>(["applied", "ignored"])`.

fix: Plan §2 #52 after the owner's answers to the open points (staging, partial resolution display, notice); a board row for the work.

problem: Owner answers on disk-as-truth (2026-10-11): (1) a file on disk without conflict markers, or deleted, is staged by yamt right away (git add / git rm), later disk changes to it likewise; (2) partly fixed on disk: the middle pane shows the disk file, each conflict still marked becomes a normal yamt conflict with arrows/x, sides unchanged, everything settled on disk counts as done; (3) a short closable notice names the file when its unsaved yamt edits are dropped.
fix: Plan §2 #52; board rows 13 (design) and 13' (build); handoff document.

problem: Owner (2026-10-11), asked about files changed before yamt starts (regenerated lock file, partial hand fixes, replayed resolutions): chose 'start from the disk whenever it differs from what git wrote' over 'only when no markers are left' and 'keep as today'. A file changed before start is treated exactly like a change made while yamt runs: fully fixed -> staged and marked resolved at once; partly fixed -> only the remaining conflicts. Accepted cost: settled changes in such a file can no longer be reviewed one by one; yamt re-runs git's merge at start to know what git wrote.
fix: plan §2 #52 amended; design V0DiskTruthDesign gets the start-up detection

problem: One conflicted path that cannot be read (EACCES, or a submodule whose `rev-parse` fails with a real git error) now makes `MergeSession::open` fail, so yamt does not start, although `refresh` treats the same read error as a warning and skips the file.
fix: On a read error in open_file, log the same `disk_unread` warning and start the file as `Seen::GitOutput` without a start look; the first refresh then retries it the way it retries any other unread file.

problem: If the read-back after a successful `git add` (and likewise in take/reset) fails, finish returns `Err(ReadFailed)` although the file is written and staged. The window then reports a failed write, and because `seen` keeps the pre-write bytes, the next refresh reports yamt's own write as an outside 'changed on disk' change.
fix: After the write has succeeded, treat a failed read-back as a warning and still return `Written`. For finish, set `seen` from the bytes just written (`fs::write` applies no filter); for take/reset, log the failure and leave `seen` for the next look.

problem: `Error::ReadFailed` becomes `IpcError::WriteFailed` with only the io message, so problemText.ts will show 'writing <path> failed: Permission denied' when yamt failed to read the file before any write.
fix: Propose `IpcError::ReadFailed { path, message }` to the orchestrator before the window half binds problemText's exhaustive switch (bindings are regenerated anyway). Until then, at least keep the session's 'cannot read' wording in `message`.

problem: Files yamt deliberately never stages (a working-tree-encoding file, a submodule that is no longer checked out) are reported as `MarkersLeft { conflicts: 0 }`. That says 'markers left: none' while meaning 'left alone', and for a UTF-16 file the count comes from parsing UTF-16 bytes, which is meaningless.
fix: Give this case its own `DiskResult` variant (e.g. `LeftAsIs`), proposed as a #53 amendment before the window half reads `conflicts`. Compute `conflicts` only for `StageWithoutMarkers` files.

problem: To settle one file, changed_on_disk builds a `Vec<Option<OnDisk>>` as long as all files, using a `disk.take()` closure, because `settle` couples its input to file order by position (its doc comment has to explain 'one per file, in file order').
fix: Let `settle` take `Vec<(usize, OnDisk)>` (file index and read). refresh then pushes only the changed files, changed_on_disk passes `vec![(index, disk)]`, and the positional doc comment goes away.

problem: commands.rs is 437 lines and crates/session/tests/describe_and_take.rs is about 415, both over the 400-line file limit (implementer open_risk).
fix: Move `IpcError`, its `From<yamt_session::Error>` and the `every_session_error_serialises…` test into `src-tauri/src/ipc_error.rs` (a separate responsibility, about 85 lines). Move describe_and_take.rs's take/reset tests into `tests/take.rs`.

problem: The public `MergeInputs<'a>` puts a lifetime into gitio's public signature (`merge_file(&self, scratch, inputs: &MergeInputs<'_>, options)`), which RS1 forbids.
fix: Drop `MergeInputs` and take the three borrowed slices as parameters: `merge_file(&self, scratch: &Path, base: &[u8], local: &[u8], remote: &[u8], options: &MergeFileOptions)`.

problem: `line_map.rs` is tracked under crates/merge-core/src/, but skill://project-map does not name `line_map`. `just map-check` therefore fails on this tree, and the report's 'map-check: ok' cannot hold for commit e11a6d3.
fix: Orchestrator: add `line_map (2-way LineMap: exact/covering)` to project-map's merge-core line, together with the other doc updates the implementer listed, before running `just check`.

problem: `Located { local: Range<u32>, remote: Range<u32> }` and `Maps::base` carry local and remote lines as bare u32. Passing `located.remote` through `local_to_base` would compile, although vision 4 makes mixing line spaces a type error.
fix: Build `Located` as `LineRange<LocalLine>` / `LineRange<RemoteLine>` in `Maps::block`/`Maps::raw`, unwrap to `Range<u32>` only at the `LineMap` call, and reuse those ranges directly in `push_conflict`.

problem: `Seen` is both the last read and the selector for the window's view, so its doc comment has to explain the double meaning, and `load` chooses the view by matching on a field named `seen`.
fix: Rename the variants to say which view they select, e.g. `ViewFromStages(OnDisk)` / `ViewFromDisk(OnDisk)`, and drop the enum-level explanation.

When a pushed base line does not end in `\n` and is not the last line of the middle, append the disk's line ending (CRLF or LF per `self.eol`). Add a seed test with a base lacking its final newline and a settled line after the block, asserting the middle text and applying ours.

problem: An unspecified `merge` attribute is always treated as the text driver, but git uses `merge.default` for such paths (merge-ll.c `find_ll_merge_driver`). With `merge.default=binary`, git leaves every conflicted text file as ours without markers, yamt's merge-file output has markers, the file counts as changed, and the first `list_files` stages every untouched conflict as ours. The design notes (line 175) list only smudge filters as start false positives that stage.
fix: Resolve the driver as git does: for an unspecified attribute, read `merge.default` (one `git config --get` in gitio) and map `binary`/`union`/`text`/other the same way as an attribute value. Add a start_from_disk case with `merge.default=binary` asserting no disk change.

problem: `merge=<name>` with no `merge.<name>.driver` configured falls back to git's text merge (merge-ll.c: 'default to the 3-way'), but start.rs:107 calls it Custom/changed. A common case is `merge=lfs` written by `git lfs track`, which does not define a driver. Such untouched files open from disk with a MarkersLeft notice. This test pins that false positive: in its hermetic repo git did a plain text merge, because mergiraf is not configured.
fix: Count a name as Custom only when `merge.<name>.driver` is configured (fall back to Text otherwise). Have the test configure `merge.mergiraf.driver` (e.g. a script that writes markers and exits 1), and add an unconfigured-name case expecting no change.

problem: Two blocks can sit inside one local→base hunk: git's zealous refine splits a conflict on ≥4 shared alnum lines both sides added. Both blocks then get the same covering base range, `push_base_lines` writes those base lines twice into the middle, and the chunks overlap in base space. That breaks the invariant that chunks are pairwise disjoint in base space (architecture §3.1). Open risk #3 names wider spans, not duplication.
fix: Clamp each chunk's base range so it starts no earlier than the previous chunk's base end (and push only the clamped lines). Add a seed test with a conflict that git splits into two blocks around 4 shared lines, asserting disjoint base ranges and applying ours on both.

problem: `read_on_disk(...)?` in `open_file` makes one unreadable conflicted path fail the whole open (the app refuses to start; before the patch it opened). Examples: permission denied, or a submodule whose `.git` file points at a missing gitdir. `refresh` skips such a file with a warn.
fix: On a read error at open, log a warn and start that file with `seen = Seen::GitOutput` (no start look). It then follows refresh's skip-and-retry path, and writes report ReadFailed.

problem: No test has inputs where histogram and myers merges differ: this test sets `histogram: true` but only checks union output, and every start_from_disk case merges the same either way. Dropping `--diff-algorithm=histogram` or mutating `version >= HISTOGRAM_SINCE` therefore survives (the implementer reports the surviving mutant).
fix: Add a start_from_disk case (or a merge_file test) on a triple whose merge-ort/histogram output differs from myers (e.g. RK13's pinned case A/B in cli/tests/merge_file.rs), and assert the untouched file reports no change.

problem: In a_section_line_repeated_elsewhere_still_applies_the_exact_text, the ours view equals local line for line, so the diff has no hunks and the repeated `dup` can never be aligned elsewhere. The test passes for any mapping that is the identity.
fix: Give remote a clean change next to the repeated line (so the settled text, and hence the ours view, differs from local around it), then assert the exact ranges and that applying ours and theirs both give the by-hand file.

problem: `finish` writes with `fs::write`, which follows a symlink. After a text file was replaced by a link and settled (`Seen::Disk(Link)`, view DiskNotText{Link}), a finish with the current version writes the user's text into the link's target, a file yamt never showed (it may be outside the repo).
fix: In `finish`, refuse when the file's seen entry is a Link/Other/Submodule (e.g. return Error::Unsupported or ChangedOnDisk), or remove the link before writing; add a test in disk_is_truth.rs.

problem: The scratch dir that holds the base/local/remote blobs is created with the default mode (0777 minus umask, usually 0755), so other local users can read the merge inputs while open runs.
fix: Create it with `std::fs::DirBuilder::new().mode(0o700)` (std `os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt`).

problem: The module map still says `commands.rs (commands ≤ 15 lines delegating to session, IpcError, one Mutex<MergeSession>)` and never names ipc_error.rs, although IpcError and its mapping from session errors now live in src-tauri/src/ipc_error.rs.
fix: Drop IpcError from the commands.rs entry and add `ipc_error.rs` (`IpcError`, mapped from `yamt_session::Error`).

problem: The MergeDriver docs describe the old attribute-only mapping. The enum doc still reads "The `merge` attribute (gitattributes(5) \"Built-in merge drivers\")" and Custom still reads "Any other driver: what it wrote cannot be known". But Custom now means only a configured `merge.<name>.driver`, an unconfigured name is Text, and Binary also comes from `merge.default=binary`.
fix: Reword the enum doc as 'the driver git used, resolved from the attribute and the merge config (merge_driver)', and Custom as 'a `merge.<name>.driver` from the config: what it wrote cannot be known'.

problem: Session NotAFile crosses as WriteFailed with a yamt-written English sentence in `message` (NOT_A_FILE). The same words are also in session lib.rs:46 `#[error("cannot write {path}: it is not a regular file")]`, so two copies can drift. The window cannot tell this refusal from an io failure, although failure wording belongs to ui/problemText.ts.
fix: Propose a structured `IpcError::NotAFile { path }` to the orchestrator before bindings are regenerated, so problemText words it. If WriteFailed is kept, define the phrase once in session and reuse it in both the `#[error]` and the IPC mapping.

problem: The doc on `base_end` ("Where the previous chunk's base lines end; the next chunk's start no earlier.") restates the field name, and its second half repeats the invariant already stated on after_previous_base.
fix: Rename the field `previous_base_end` and delete the doc comment.

problem: Settlement mixes actions (Add, Remove, LeaveAsIs) with a result name (MarkersLeft), and LeaveAsIs/LeftAsIs differ from DiskResult by one word while MarkersLeft matches it exactly.
fix: Rename `Settlement::MarkersLeft` to `LeaveWithMarkers { conflicts }` so all four variants read as actions.

problem: `Repo::merge_config` and `attributes` read the developer's global config, but the conflict repos were merged without it. So `cargo test` fails on a machine whose ~/.gitconfig sets `merge.default=binary` (45 failures, among them every disk_is_truth test, e.g. `an_unchanged_disk_reports_nothing…` gets `MarkersLeft{2}`) or has mergiraf's recommended global driver plus attributes (45). A global `merge.<name>.driver` alone breaks `no_config == MergeConfig::default()`.
fix: Run the gitio/session test binaries with the user and system config isolated, e.g. export `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<empty dir>` in `just test` (and document it for bare `cargo test`). In the gitio test, assert only what the repo-local keys add (`config.default == binary`, `config.drivers.last() == mergiraf`), not equality with the default.

problem: `merge_file_returns_the_merge_with_one_or_two_conflicts` passes only because this machine's ~/.gitconfig sets `merge.conflictstyle=zdiff3`. With no global config (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null), git's merge style joins `A b c d E`/`X b c d Y` into one block and the `count == 2` assert fails. Any CI or fresh machine sees a red suite. The test dates from round 1.
fix:
Use a two-block input that splits under every conflict style, e.g. hunks separated by four or more alnum lines like `a
bb
cc
dd
ee
f
`, or set `merge.conflictStyle` in the conflict repo's config (`Setup::config`).

problem: `a_configured_merge_driver_with_markers_opens_from_disk_at_the_first_list` still passes if the `config.drivers.contains(name)` lookup is deleted: `mergiraf` then falls back to Text, git's text merge of OURS/THEIRS differs from the driver's `local`/`remote` block, so the file is Changed and gives `MarkersLeft{1}` + Disk view anyway. No test proves that a configured name gives Custom.
fix: Make the driver write exactly git's text merge, e.g. `git merge-file -L ours -L base -L theirs %A %O %B; exit 1`. Then Custom (always Changed → MarkersLeft, Disk view) and Text (Untouched → Stages view) give different results, and keep the assertions as they are.

problem: #533 is only half-fixed. Remote's `dup`→`DUP` substitution keeps the ours view and local line for line the same length, so an identity ours→local mapping (and any off-by-N that is 0 here) still yields the asserted `(2,1)` ranges and the exact apply results. Only a content-search mapping is caught.
fix:
Make remote's clean change insert a line before the block, e.g. remote `DUP
new
mid
other
end
` with the settled `new` line in the disk text. The ours line of the block then sits at view line 3 but at local line 2, and the identity mapping fails the range and apply asserts.

problem: `just test` and `just mutants` (line 110) isolate the config files but leave GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS/GIT_CONFIG_COUNT set. Config passed through the environment, which RK19 names explicitly (e.g. a `just check` run from a hook under `git -c merge.default=binary …`), therefore still reaches yamt's Repo::merge_config/attributes in the gitio and session tests, while the conflict repos were merged without it. scripts/git-sandbox.sh:35 unsets exactly these two variables.
fix: Prefix both recipes with `env -u GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/nonexistent`, the same set git-sandbox.sh uses.

problem: The isolation env is written twice (test:14 and mutants:110), and the two copies can drift. The mutants copy is also `export`ed for the whole script, so the user's config is dropped from `git diff {{ base }}` too, and XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/nonexistent reaches pnpm/Stryker. pnpm reads its global rc from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and the TS half never runs git.
fix: Define one variable (e.g. `hermetic_git := "env -u GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/nonexistent"`) and use it as a prefix only on `cargo nextest run` and on the `cargo mutants` line.

problem: #594 SIDE_PANE adds a second way to map a side to its pane, while drag.ts:38, gap.ts:19 and strips.ts:200-202 still spell the same fact as `side === "local" ? …left : …right` ternaries.
fix: Replace those three ternaries with `views[SIDE_PANE[side]]` / `row[SIDE_PANE[side]]` so the mapping exists once.

problem: #595 `alone(mark).remembered` uses a constructor to read "the change this mark points at or remembers", so the reader has to work out that building an alone mark is just a getter.
fix: Add `markedId(mark): Chunk["id"] | null` in navigation.ts, use it in settled, and build alone() on top of it.

problem: #596 `#show` both sets the mark and moves DOM focus. Elsewhere in editor/, show* (showStatuses, showCovered, showFindSpace) only pushes display state, so the name hides the focus move.
fix: Rename `#show` to `#focusOn(side, mark)`.

problem: #597 #54 'Ctrl/Cmd+scroll over a side focuses that side and its next/previous waiting change' and 'Ctrl/Cmd+scroll over the middle scrolls as usual' (WebKit step 10) have never been observed; the only evidence is wheel.test.ts, which tests the pure burst rule and would pass if the wheel listener in SideFocus were deleted or never got ctrlKey in WebKitGTK.
fix: No code change: the verifier pastes a real X11 run in the WebKitGTK app (e.g. xdotool keydown ctrl + click 5/4 over the right pane, then over the middle): right pane focused with its next waiting change outlined, one change per notch, middle scrolls without zoom.

problem: #598 #54 'not while a "Mark resolved?" or quit question is open' has no evidence at all: no unit test and no WebKit step exercises Ctrl+Z with store.question set, so deleting the `question.value === null` condition would go unnoticed.
fix: Add the step to the verifier's WebKit run (Mark resolved with conflicts left, press Ctrl+Z while the question shows: middle text and summary unchanged), or extract the gate into a pure ui/ predicate with a node test covering shown/hidden × question/no question.

problem: #599 The capture-phase mousedown on scrollDOM also fires for presses on the scrollbar, so dragging a side's scrollbar retargets that side's mark to whatever change lies beside the thumb (or clears it to alone) although #54 rule 1 only speaks of clicks in the pane and on a change block; the next Enter then decides a different change than the one the user had outlined.
fix: Return early when `event.target === view.scrollDOM` (scrollbar presses target the scroller itself; text, the empty area and the gutters do not), and add the case to the open-risk note.

problem: #600 historyCommand matches only `event.key`, so on a non-Latin layout (Ctrl+Z gives key 'я' on Russian) undo works in the middle — CodeMirror falls back to the keyCode — but does nothing from a side pane or anywhere else, contradicting #54 'undoes anywhere in the shown file's window'.
fix: When `event.key` is not a single ASCII letter, fall back to `event.code` ('KeyZ'/'KeyY') as CodeMirror's runHandlers does with keyCode, and add a historyKey.test row with key 'я', code 'KeyZ'.

problem: #601 After an icon click, a drag or a Ctrl/Cmd+click with the keyboard on a side, the outline moves on (settled) but the view never reveals it, so the outline can land off screen and the next Enter applies a change the user cannot see; #54 says a newly focused change off screen 'lands as WebStorm places a difference', while the brief's A5 says 'clicks never scroll' and the implementer chose no reveal.
fix: Have the orchestrator settle #54 vs A5 with the owner; if #54 holds, after #decide in #act reveal the mark of the side that still has DOM focus (expose SideFocus.reveal for that side; it is null when already on screen).

problem: #602 #54 says 'waiting changes only beyond the screen in the pressed direction → nothing', which read literally means Down with changes only below the screen does nothing, while the brief, #587 and the patch (fromScreen has no lower bound; stepAlone returns null only when changes wait only above) jump down to the first one below; the verifier reading #54 as acceptance could fail correct behaviour.
fix: Reword the plan clause to 'waiting changes only above the visible area for Down (below it for Up) → nothing', matching #587 and navigation.test 'a side alone with waiting changes only above the area stays put'.

problem: #603 decided() hands the keyboard over whenever the focused side has nothing waiting, even when the decision was on the other side and the focused side was already empty (e.g. ArrowLeft onto a finished local, then a click on a remote icon moves the keyboard to remote), which breaks #589's 'the keyboard stays where it was'.
fix: Hand over only when the focused side had a waiting change before the decision (compare hasWaiting before and after #dispatch in #decide).

problem: #604 A Ctrl/Cmd+click on a side that hits no waiting change is skipped by #pressed, but modClick does not consume it, so the browser focuses the side with its old mark still outlined instead of the side alone (rule 1).
fix: Skip the mod-click in #pressed only when changeAt finds a waiting change; otherwise fall through and set the side alone.

problem: #605 Implementer-reported: WebKit moves DOM focus to DIV.cm-scroller when a side's scrollbar is pressed; the mark stays but the side loses cm-focused, so no outline and keys do not reach the side until the next click (browser behaviour, outside #599).
fix: Follow-up: on focus landing on a side's scrollDOM, hand it to its contentDOM (preventScroll).

problem: #606 Implementer-reported: Ctrl/Cmd+click within POINT_HIT_PX of a zero-line change's bar is skipped by #pressed (changeAt hits it) but not consumed by modClick (openBlockAt needs len > 0), so the side gets focus with its old mark.
fix: Follow-up: one hit test for both, or #pressed defers to modClick's own result.

problem: #607 `decided()` calls `#reveal(focused)` whenever no handover happens, even when the decision left that side's mark unchanged. Example: the keyboard is on the left with change c5 outlined; the user wheel-scrolls away and clicks the apply icon of another change, on either side. The view jumps back to c5. Plan §2 #54 moves the view only for 'a newly focused change', and #590 rejected re-placing a change that was not newly focused.
fix: Read the focused side's mark before `#dispatch` (for example, have SideFocus wrap the decision as `decide(run: () => void)` and take both the states snapshot and the marks itself, so #decide no longer reads the field for it). Call `#reveal` only when `markedId` of the focused side changed.

problem: #608 letterOf falls back to `code` for any `key` that is not a Latin letter, including ASCII punctuation, so Dvorak Ctrl+; (key ';', code 'KeyZ') undoes. CodeMirror's keyCode fallback does not do this, although the comment at :21-22 says the behaviour is like CodeMirror's.
fix: Fall back to `code` only when `key` is a single non-ASCII character (for example `/^[^\x00-\x7f]$/u`), and add a Dvorak row: key ';' with code 'KeyZ' gives null.

problem: #609 decided() reveals the focused side's mark after every decision, even when the decision did not move it. Example: keyboard on the left with change A outlined, the view wheel-scrolled down, then a click on the apply icon of another left change B (or Ctrl+click on B, a drag, or a remote icon). A still waits, so the mark stays on A and #reveal scrolls all panes back to A, away from the change the user just clicked. #54 reveals only a *newly focused* change, and the keyboard 'stays where it was'.
fix: Capture the focused side's mark before the dispatch (e.g. in #decide next to `before`, or have SideFocus snapshot `#mark(side)` for both sides) and call #reveal(focused) only when the settled mark differs from it.

problem: #610 Nothing at unit level covers the reveal-or-handover branch in decided() (#601). Deleting `else if (focused !== null) this.#reveal(focused)` or revealing unconditionally would pass every test. WebKit step 2 clicked only the outlined change's icon, so it never exercised the unmoved-mark case behind finding 1.
fix: Move the decision into a pure navigation.ts helper, e.g. `afterDecisionFocus({ beforeMark, afterMark, handover }) → 'handover' | 'reveal' | 'stay'`. Unit-test it for: mark moved, mark unchanged, mark became alone, and handover.

problem: #611 The fallback to `code` also fires for Latin layouts whose KeyZ/KeyY key produces a non-letter. On Dvorak, physical KeyZ gives ';', so Ctrl+; undoes from a side pane. CodeMirror's keyCode fallback, which the comment cites, would map that key to ';'.
fix: Fall back to `code` only when `key` is a single non-ASCII letter (`/^\p{L}$/u` and not LATIN_LETTER), and add a row asserting that key ';' with code 'KeyZ' gives null.

problem: #612 Two statements in architecture.md no longer match the code. Lines 522-523 say historyKey falls back to the physical key 'only when the layout gives no Latin letter', but Dvorak's ';' gives no Latin letter and no longer falls back. Lines 515-516 list the navigation.ts rules without the new decision rule: reveal only when the outline moved to another change, otherwise stay; handover wins.
fix: The orchestrator (docs are outside `Owned`) should change line 522 to 'only when the layout gives a single non-Latin letter'. It should also add 'after a decision: hand over, reveal a newly focused change, or stay' to the navigation.ts list at 515. — applied by the orchestrator.

problem: #613 `afterDecisionFocus` returns the module-private type `AfterDecision`. That name reads as the return type of the unrelated `afterDecision` (navigation.ts:44, the next id after a decision).
fix: Rename the type to `FocusAfterDecision` (or `AfterDecisionFocus`) to match the function that returns it.

problem: #614 `/^\p{L}$/u` rejects combining vowel signs. On Hindi/Marathi InScript, physical KeyZ gives `key` 'ॆ' (U+0946, category Mn; checked with node: \p{L} false), so Ctrl+Z in a side pane no longer undoes. Rework 1 handled that layout, and CodeMirror's keyCode fallback still handles it in the middle pane, against #54's 'on any keyboard layout' (the regex is the brief's own prescription).
fix: Fall back to `code` for any single non-ASCII key, e.g. `/^[\p{L}\p{M}]$/u` or `/^\P{ASCII}$/u` in place of ANY_LETTER, and add a row: key 'ॆ' with code 'KeyZ' gives "undo".

problem: #615 The #607 fix depends on `beforeMark` being read before `dispatch()`, and no automated test covers that order. Moving line 114 below line 115 makes every decision 'stay' (never reveal), and every node test still passes; only the manual WebKit steps 3 and 4 would notice.
fix: Add an `editor/**/*.browser.test.ts` case that builds a MergeController on the magic-keys fixture, focuses the left pane on a change, presses Enter and expects the left mark to move with scrollTop changed. In the same test, deciding another change through the controller's icon path should leave the mark and scrollTop unchanged. Or log the gap as a follow-up next to #605/#606.

problem: #616 The row `key 'f', code 'KeyY'` returns null with or without the fix, because 'f' is a Latin letter and wins in the first branch, so it does not show the Dvorak rule.
fix: Drop the row or replace it with a non-letter on KeyY (e.g. key '-' with code 'KeyY' gives null).

problem: #617 Stryker NoCoverage on the wave's lines: `current()?.controller` → `current().controller` at :70-73 (applyAllNonConflicting, undo, redo, historyKey) — with no controller yet (file still loading) a toolbar click or Ctrl+Z would throw; no test covers the guard.
fix: Row 1''': a useMergeController test calling the handle before a controller exists (no throw, historyKey false).

problem: #618 Survivors `() => undefined` on the delegations at :70-73 and `?? false → ?? true` at :73: pure forwarding (the only caller ignores historyKey's return); the real-app run exercised Ctrl+Z through it.

problem: #620 One X11 mouse notch in WebKitGTK is deltaY 96 (deltaMode 0) while WHEEL_STEP_PX is 100: slow notches step once each (the first event of a burst steps), but a fast spin within one burst steps about every second notch. Unmeasured on Wayland and macOS.

problem: #630 Owner 2026-10-12: "ctrl/cmd+rightclick on a block = ignore. ctrl/cmd+click on the apply icon applies that side and ignores the other side at same time (on conflict). ctrl/cmd+click on ignore ignores the clicked side and applies the other side". WebStorm source (intellij-community ThreesideMergeHighlighters.createApplyRenderer/createIgnoreRenderer, ctrlPressed → MergeConflictModel.replaceChange/ignoreChange resolveChange=true): Ctrl+click on apply = apply and resolve the whole conflict (matches); Ctrl+click on ignore = mark the whole conflict resolved without applying the other side (differs: the owner's applies the other side); Ctrl+right-click on text has no WebStorm counterpart. Supersedes plan #46's rejection of WebStorm's Ctrl+click on the icon.

problem: #631 Owner answers 2026-10-12 to #630: (1) Ctrl/Cmd+click on a conflict's ignore icon ignores that side and takes the other — the owner's version, not WebStorm's ignore-both; (2) holding Ctrl/Cmd while dragging over several icons decides both sides of every covered conflict, one undo step; (3) the conflict icons' hover hint gains a line ("Ctrl+click: also ignore the other side" / "Ctrl+click: also take the other side", ⌘ on macOS), only while the other side is still open.
fix: Plan §2 #55.

problem: #632 Two modules state separately when a Ctrl/Cmd click also decides the other side: the hint uses `chunk.kind === "Conflict" && isSideOpen(other)` here, the action uses `chunk.kind === "Conflict"` in sideDecisions (apply.ts:104) plus chainedChanges' isSideOpen guard, so a later change to one (e.g. including BothSame) silently makes the hint promise something the click does not do.
fix: Add one predicate next to the status rules (e.g. `decidesOtherSide(chunk, status, side)` in status.ts or apply.ts) and use it for both `otherWaits` and the reach-'conflict' branch of sideDecisions.

problem: #633 #pressed decides on its own whether modClicks will consume this press (`changeAt` hit && !readOnly && isModHeld). That is the rule duplication behind #606: only the hit test was unified, the consume condition still lives in two places and can drift again.
fix: In #pressed, skip when `!this.#sources.readOnly && modClickAction(this.#sources.rows(), { side, y, click: event, platform }) !== null`, so the press handler asks the same function modClicks acts on.

problem: #634 The row-rebuild check compares derived title strings, so `titles` is threaded through PlacedArrow and ArrowRow and a titles object plus template strings is built for every visible arrow on every frame, when the input fact is the boolean `arrow.otherWaits` (the platform never changes).
fix: Store `otherWaits` in ArrowRow, compare `row.otherWaits === arrow.otherWaits` in sameShape, and call `arrowTitles(arrow, platform)` only inside arrowRow when a row is (re)built; drop `titles` from PlacedArrow.

problem: #635 The comment's second clause ('on macOS Ctrl+click is the system's secondary click') now sits above isMac, but it justifies isModHeld's `metaKey && !ctrlKey` rule two functions below.
fix: Keep the CodeMirror `browser.mac` reference above isMac and move the secondary-click clause back above the return in isModHeld.

problem: #636 A Ctrl/Cmd drag ends with different spans than clicking each change. When an applied span's `to` touches a later zero-line span that the same action also applies, the composed one-shot mapping moves the earlier `to` past the later insertion. Ctrl/Cmd+ignore dragged over [conflict, touching zero-line conflict] gives spans [2,8),[8,8) where clicking each gives [2,5),[5,8). This path is new in this slice. The apply-drag variant over [LocalOnly, touching zero-line conflict] has the same problem and already existed before it.
fix: Have the action transaction carry the spans the chained throwaway state ends with (for example a `placeSpans` effect that `updateSpans` takes as given, like `restoreSpans`) instead of re-mapping the composed ChangeSet. Add the apply-drag and Ctrl-ignore touching variants to the apply.test.ts:944 case.

problem: #637 The hint test checks only `arrowTitles`, so it still passes with today's `sameShape`: removing the title comparison at strips.ts:147-148 brings back the stale two-line title after the other side is ignored, and no node test fails. The brief requires a test that fails with today's `sameShape`; the only evidence now is WebKit step 4.
fix: Turn the row-reuse decision into a pure exported function over plain data (mode, titles, layout). Test that a row built while the other side was pending is not reused once that side is ignored.

problem: #638 The name `LETTER_OR_VOWEL_SIGN` says vowel signs, but `\p{M}` matches every combining mark (enclosing marks, diacritics), so the name understates what falls back to the physical key.

problem: #642 The action transaction still carries one setStatus per decision, but nothing reads them: the field takes placeSpans and ignores setStatus when both are present (chunkField.ts:117-118), the side-pane push compares field statuses (index.ts:206-209), and the undo inversion fires on placeSpans anyway (chunkField.ts:122). The brief's two reasons for keeping them do not hold, so the transaction states the status twice and one copy is never used.
fix: Return only `placeSpans.of(state.field(target.field))` as the chain's effects, keep setStatus only in the throwaway `state.update` (drop the `effects` accumulator), and record this in CM6 step 2. If the orchestrator wants to keep the brief's instruction, say there why the copies stay.

problem: #643 Four cm6 rules no longer describe the code. CM1 L19-20: the applied-span `+1` push now applies only to transactions without placeSpans. CM2 L24-27: status no longer changes only through setStatus, and undo restores it through a placeSpans snapshot, not an inverted setStatus. CM6 L45: step 2's `effects: setStatus…` should be placeSpans. CM7 L52-56 does not say the action carries the chain's final spans. The implementer's deviations name CM1, CM2 and CM7 but not CM6.
fix: Orchestrator rewrites them: CM1 adds 'a transaction carrying `placeSpans` (an action's chained final spans, or undo/redo's snapshot) sets the spans as given; the mapping rules apply to every other transaction, including each throwaway step'. CM2 becomes 'per-transaction status changes go through `setStatus`; spans and statuses are set wholesale only by `placeSpans`, which `invertedEffects` also uses to restore them on undo'. CM6 step 2 becomes `{ changes?, effects: placeSpans, userEvent }`. CM7 adds 'and the chain's final spans as `placeSpans` in that same transaction'.

problem: #644 The state-ownership rows for chunk positions and chunk status (project-map L98-99, architecture.md L429-430) still say positions are 'mapped per CM1, restored on undo' and status is 'changed only by a StateEffect registered with invertedEffects'. Actions now set both wholesale through the exported placeSpans, and the implementer's deviations do not list these rows.
fix: Orchestrator updates both tables: positions are 'mapped per CM1, or set as given by `placeSpans` (an action's chained final spans; undo's snapshot via `invertedEffects`)', and status is 'setStatus per transaction, or wholesale by `placeSpans` (actions and undo)'.

problem: #645 After the unification the field `Arrow.otherWaits` (also on ArrowShape and ArrowRow) holds `decidesOtherSide(...)`, which is false for a BothSame or LocalOnly change whose other side still waits. So the same fact has two names, and one of them misdescribes non-conflicts.
fix: Rename the field to `decidesOther` everywhere (gap.ts, strips.ts, gap.test.ts) so it reads as the predicate it holds.

problem: #646 The same `[from, to]` pairs helper now exists three times: module-level `spanPairs` (L975) and two test-local `spans` (L463, L954). The rework added the module-level one next to a local copy it duplicates.
fix: Keep the module-level `spanPairs` and replace both local `spans` functions with it.

problem: #647 The per-step setStatus effects in the dispatched action transaction are no longer read by anything: chunkField.update returns placed.value and skips updateSpans, invertedEffects fires on placeSpans alone, and the side-pane push compares field status identity (index.ts:204-212). The implementer's proposed CM2 wording ('setStatus stays … for the side panes' status push and for the inversion trigger') would therefore put a false rule into cm6-rules.
fix: Either have chainedChanges return only placeSpans for the action step, or keep the effects and word CM2 as 'actions carry placeSpans (the field's only input then); setStatus in the action step is informational'. Do not claim setStatus drives the push or the inversion.

problem: #648 `spanPairs` was added at file level, but identical local `spans` helpers remain in the tests at lines 463 and 954, so the file now has three copies of the same span-pair reader.

problem: #649 The row says the spans are 'mapped per CM1 (`-1`; `to` `+1` only when a range ends mid-line)', but mapSpans (chunkField.ts:58-61) also maps `to` with +1 for a span applied in the transaction and raises later spans' `from` to it, so 'only' contradicts CM1's applied-span rule.

problem: #650 '`setStatus` within a transaction, or wholesale by `placeSpans` (actions and undo)' suggests any dispatched transaction may carry setStatus (after R2 only the throwaway chain steps do, CM2), and it leaves out the third writer: a user edit that deletes an open block sets DELETED_BY_USER (chunkField.ts:91-93, CM8).

problem: #651 The owner cell lists only '`setStatus` … (each throwaway step of an action's chain), or wholesale by `placeSpans` (actions and undo)' as writers, so a reader asking 'what can change status?' misses the CM8 collapse (collapsedByUser → DELETED_BY_USER in updateSpans) that CM2 names.

problem: #652 The now-shared `spanPairs` helper is defined at line 969, between tests, while its first users are at 475/480 and the other span/status helpers (`spanAt`, `statuses`, `centerText`) are at lines 87-190; a reader of the line-475 test has to search for it.

problem: #666 The two `#[serde(default)]` attributes make the generated `StoredSettings` `{ theme?: Theme; keys?: … }`, although Rust always sends both fields and nothing in Rust deserialises StoredSettings except the IPC `current` argument (the file is parsed field by field through `file::entry`). The web build (`bindingsOf(stored: StoredSettings["keys"])`, `read.stored.theme`) would have to handle `undefined` and keep a second copy of the defaults, and a window that sends `{}` silently creates a file from Dark/no keys.
fix: Remove both `#[serde(default)]` attributes before the web builds start, so the generated fields are required in both directions; the file's missing-entry defaults stay in `file::entry`. Answer to the orchestrator's question: yes, change it now; it is a contract edit the orchestrator owns.

problem: #667 (same as previous) `#[serde(default)]` on StoredSettings' fields has no Rust user: file.rs:106-118 defaults missing file entries itself. Its only effect is that the generated TS reads `theme?: Theme; keys?: {…}` (bindings.ts:205-208) on a reply that Rust always fills, so web build 1 must either add `??` defaults or cast in domain.ts. Also, a `current` that leaves out `keys` would silently create a file from the defaults.
fix: Drop both `#[serde(default)]` attributes (the orchestrator amends the fixed contract before web build 1 starts) so the generated fields are required. The file parser's own defaulting stays as it is.

problem: #668 When the settings path is a dangling symlink (a dotfiles link whose target does not exist yet), `canonicalize` fails and the code falls back to the link path, and `load` reads it as missing. A read or change then renames a regular file over the link, which goes against rule 6 ("the link stays a link"). The implementer listed this as an open risk, but no fix or test covers it.
fix: In `write_text`, when `fs::symlink_metadata(path)` says symlink, resolve it with `fs::read_link` (joining a relative target onto `path.parent()`) instead of `canonicalize`, and add a test `a_dangling_settings_symlink_creates_its_target_and_stays_a_link`.

problem: #669 `contains(r#"dataset.theme = "light""#)` would still pass if the script set the attribute on `document.body` or some other element, so the unit test does not pin the `<html>` target that rule 10 requires (only the smoke does).
fix: Use `assert_eq!(start_script(Theme::Light), r#"document.documentElement.dataset.theme = "light";"#)` and the same for Dark.

problem: #670 `Loaded` keeps theme and keys twice, as `entries["theme"/"keys"]` and as `stored`. set_theme, set_keys, put_keys and from_settings must keep both copies in step (lines 21-62), and the doc comment exists to explain this pairing.
fix: Have `parsed` remove `theme`/`keys` from the map with `serde_json::from_value` (as the brief says), then hold `Loaded { others: Map<String, Value>, stored: StoredSettings }` with one `fn entries(self) -> Map` used by `write_entries`. The setters then change only `stored`, and put_keys and the comment go away.

problem: #671 The words "dark"/"light" are spelled in three places that nothing ties together: serde's `rename_all = "lowercase"` (lib.rs:16), `theme_name` here, and `start_script`'s match (src-tauri/src/window.rs:79-83).
fix: Add one `pub fn name(self) -> &'static str` on `Theme` in yamt-settings (a contract addition for the orchestrator to approve), with a unit test that it equals `serde_json::to_value(theme)`, and call it from both file.rs and start_script.

problem: #672 `start_theme<R: Runtime>` is generic but only ever built for `tauri::Wry`: its one caller is open_and_wait with `App<Wry>`.
fix: Make the parameter `&PathResolver<tauri::Wry>` and drop the type parameter.

problem: #673 The patch adds `docs/slices/briefs/3.S-settings-view.md` and `3.S-settings-web.md`, which are outside Owned and missing from the implementer's files_changed. It also leaves out Cargo.lock, which files_changed lists and which the working tree already holds updated (yamt-settings package, plus yamt-app's dependency at Cargo.lock:4611).
fix: Commit the two briefs separately as the orchestrator's own files, and stage Cargo.lock with this slice.

problem: #674 `link_target` resolves only one symlink hop. With `settings.json` → link B → existing dotfile C, the rename replaces link B with a regular file, so C silently stops getting changes. Round 1's `canonicalize` followed that chain, so this is a regression against rule 6 ('write to its resolved target so the link stays a link'), and the doc comment on `write_text` (line 98) overstates what the code does.
fix: Follow `read_link` in a loop while `symlink_metadata` says symlink, bounded by a named const (e.g. 40, Linux's MAXSYMLINKS) so a cycle cannot hang. Add a test `a_chain_of_settings_symlinks_stays_links_and_writes_the_last_target` (link → link → file: both stay links, and the file holds the change).

problem: #675 (same as previous) `link_target` follows only one link. When the settings link points to a second link (a dotfiles chain), the rename replaces that second link with a regular file. That breaks rule 6's 'write to its resolved target', a case round 1's `canonicalize` handled whenever the last file existed (implementer open risk 1, judged here as a regression).
fix: Keep calling `fs::read_link` while `symlink_metadata` reports a symlink. Join each relative target onto the current link's folder, and stop with an error after a named limit (e.g. `const MAX_LINK_HOPS: usize = 40`, Linux's MAXSYMLINKS) so a cycle cannot loop forever. Add a test with a link → link → file chain that checks both links are still links.

problem: #676 `entries()` always writes `theme`, so a `set_keys` on a hand-written file without a `theme` entry now adds `"theme": "dark"`. Round 1 left that entry out, and architecture §3.6 and brief rule 5 say a change replaces only one entry. The value means the same, but the file gains a line.
fix: Reword architecture.md §3.6 (line 362) to say a change always writes `theme` and writes `keys` when non-empty; the code needs no change.

problem: #677 `link_target` returns `path` itself when `path` is not a link, so the name promises a link's target and the doc comment has to correct it.
fix: Name it for what it returns, the file the bytes go into (e.g. `file_to_write`), and cut the doc comment to the dangling-target case.

problem: #678 `for _ in 0..MAX_LINK_HOPS` follows at most 40 links and never checks the 40th target. A chain of exactly 40 links, which Linux reads fine, fails to write with the message "more than 40 symlinks in a row". That contradicts the error text, the const's comment ('more links in a row than this') and MAXSYMLINKS, and the same file is readable but not writable.
fix: Loop `for _ in 0..=MAX_LINK_HOPS` so that 40 links are followed and the 41st is refused, which matches both the message and Linux's limit.

problem: #679 (same as previous) `for _ in 0..MAX_LINK_HOPS` follows at most 39 links before it must reach a non-link. A chain of exactly 40 links, which the kernel and so `load` accept, fails the write with "more than 40 symlinks in a row". This contradicts both the error text and the doc on `MAX_LINK_HOPS` ("more links in a row than this is a cycle").
fix: Iterate `0..=MAX_LINK_HOPS`, so 40 links resolve and the 41st errors, matching Linux's MAXSYMLINKS.

problem: #680 The crate guide still says 'Tests are integration tests on temp folders in `tests/`', but this rework adds a unit test in file.rs (`file::tests::a_symlink_cycle_…`). A reader looking for the cycle test is sent to the wrong place.
fix: Change the sentence to say tests are integration tests in `tests/`, plus the symlink-cycle unit test in `file.rs`, which the public API cannot reach because `read` fails first.

problem: #681 The cycle test is a unit test in src/, but crates/settings/AGENTS.md says tests are integration tests on temp folders in `tests/`. The reason given in the report, that the hop limit cannot be reached through the public API, is wrong: `relocate` → `places::record_location` calls `write_text(&self.location_file, …)` without reading first, so a `settings-location` link cycle reaches `file_to_write`'s limit and is the case users would actually see.
fix: Move the test to tests/relocate.rs. Make `settings-location` one of two links that point at each other, call `relocate` to an absolute elsewhere path, and assert `Error::WriteFailed { path }` equal to the location file, that both entries are still symlinks, and that the config folder has no temp file. Then delete the `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` from file.rs.

problem: #682 The brief fixes `export type KeyName` as public surface for the next build, but KeyName is neither exported nor re-exported from ipc/index.ts. The stated reason, that knip fails on an export nobody imports, does not hold: package.json's knip config makes `**/*.test.ts` an entry, which is why ACTION_PLACES, imported only by keyText.test.ts, passes.
fix: Export KeyName from keys.ts and re-export it from ipc/index.ts, then import it in ipc/keys.test.ts (for example to type the parse helper's expected name) so knip sees a user.

problem: #683 The DEFAULT_KEYS test cites sources this patch deletes or rewires: sideFocus.ts SIDE_KEYS is gone, historyKey.ts and the find.ts keymap now read DEFAULT_KEYS themselves, and indentWithTab is gone. A reader following the citations finds nothing, or finds the code under test.

problem: #684 After the move, this file tests only sideKeyCommands from sideKeys.ts and nothing in sideFocus.ts, so a reader looking for the side keymap's tests next to sideKeys.ts finds none.
fix: Rename it to editor/internal/sideKeys.test.ts and report the rename for the project map.

problem: #685 use() replaces settings with a fresh object on every reply, so every window focus produces a new `preferences` value even when the file did not change. Every opened file then reconfigures four compartments in all three panes, and a dismissed key-problem bar comes back with an error log line.
fix: In use(), keep settings.value and skip report() when read.path and read.stored equal those already in use (compare the stored theme and the keyText lists), so only a real change moves preferences and problems.

problem: #686 Three compartments (theme, find keys, middle keys) are placed and reconfigured in pane.ts. The side-key compartment is placed in editor/index.ts:164 and reconfigured here through a callback into the controller. Answering 'what changes the side keys?' therefore means tracing index.ts → pane.ts → index.ts#sideKeys → sideKeys.ts.
fix: Have MergeController.setPreferences dispatch sideKeysCompartment.reconfigure to the side views itself and drop the callback parameter, so showPreferences covers only the compartments pane.ts places.

problem: #687 The function named `use` is not a composable, yet in ui/ the `use*` prefix marks composables.
fix: Rename it to `adopt` (or `applyRead`).

problem: #688 FixtureSettings is exported but nothing outside fixtureSettings.ts imports it.
fix: Drop the `export`, or inline `Pick<ChunkSource, …>` as createFixtureSettings' return type.

problem: #689 Every middle binding, Indent and Outdent included, now has preventDefault: true. In a read-only Result pane indentMore and indentLess refuse (state.readOnly), but CodeMirror still prevents the default, so Tab no longer moves focus out of that pane. The old indentWithTab had no preventDefault.
fix: Set preventDefault only on the undo/redo entries of MIDDLE_COMMANDS, as historyKeymap did; leave indent and outdent without it, as indentWithTab did. Add a pane.test case: a readOnlyCenter Tab binding leaves the key unhandled.

problem: #690 [INFERENCE] When Undo/Redo are rebound away from Mod-z, nothing binds or prevents Mod-z in the middle. A native undo (macOS Tauri's Edit menu Undo, or any WebKit Undo command) fires beforeinput 'historyUndo', and history()'s own handler turns that into a CodeMirror undo (@codemirror/commands dist/index.js:267-271). So Mod-z can still undo there, against item 11 and real-app step 3. pane.test only inspects the keymap facet and cannot see this.
fix: Add a Prec.highest EditorView.domEventHandlers({ beforeinput }) in the center pane that calls preventDefault and returns true for 'historyUndo'/'historyRedo', so undo comes only from the bound keys and the toolbar. Have real-app step 3 press Ctrl+Z after typing text in the middle, not only after an apply.

problem: #691 use() reports key problems on every successful read. Every window focus with a hand-edited 'twice' or 'unreadable' file therefore overwrites whatever problem is shown (e.g. a failed Finish), brings the bar back after the user dismissed it, and logs at error level again.
fix: Report key problems only when they differ from the settings in use (compare with target.settings.value.keys.problems before assigning). Add a store test: a second identical load after dismissProblem leaves problem null.

problem: #692 Settings replies are applied in arrival order with no sequencing. A focus-triggered loadSettings that resolves after a later setTheme/setKeys/moveSettings reply puts the older file state back (for example the old path after a move). editKeys also computes its changes before the clash question and sends them after the answer, even if a focus reload changed the bindings meanwhile.
fix: Keep a call counter like State.latestOpen and apply a reply only when no later settings call has started. In editKeys, run planKeyEdit again on the current bindings after the question is answered.

problem: #693 No test exercises showPreferences, the reconfigure path behind setPreferences (items 5 and 11). useMergeController.test mocks MergeController, and pane.test only builds fresh states. A showPreferences that skipped the side panes, the theme compartment or the find keys would pass every test.
fix: Extract the effects per pane kind into a pure function, e.g. preferenceEffects(kind, settings, sideKeys). Test that applying them to a center and a side state flips EditorView.darkTheme, rebinds side 'a' and find F10, and moves middle undo to Alt-Backspace.

problem: #694 parseKey accepts Shift before a non-letter character ('Shift-1', 'Shift-?'), which keyOfEvent never produces. 'Shift-1' never fires, and 'Shift-?' fires in the panes but never for window-wide undo/redo, yet neither is reported as unreadable.
fix: Refuse 'Shift-' before a one-character name that is not a letter (isLetter), add both texts to the 'anything else is refused' test, and let bindingsOf report them as 'unreadable'.

problem: #695 The fake setKeys replaces the file's whole key map with the changed actions, not Rust's per-action merge. The 'each key edit' test therefore expects the third call's current to lack the apply entry that a real reply would keep.
fix: Merge the changes into the previous reply's keys the way crates/settings set_keys does, or back the store test with createFixtureSettings().

problem: #696 The comment says the browser's own undo arrives on 'WebKit: Ctrl/Cmd+Z when no binding prevents the key', but the implementer's own WebKitGTK run saw an unprevented Ctrl+Z send no `historyUndo` at all, so the comment states as fact a path that was observed not to exist and does not source the path it actually guards.
fix: Reword the first line to name the path the guard is for (the browser's own Undo/Redo command, e.g. macOS Edit ▸ Undo or Cmd+Z in WKWebView when Undo is bound elsewhere, finding #690) and keep only the verified @codemirror/commands citation; drop the generic 'WebKit: Ctrl/Cmd+Z' claim.

problem: #697 The failure branch of `send` repeats `report`'s whole body (`logProblem` plus assigning `target.problem.value`) instead of choosing between the two existing helpers.
fix: Write it as `if (latest) { report(target, failure); } else { logProblem(failure); }`.

problem: #698 The only #690 test (pane.test.ts:356) calls the pure `refuseNativeHistory` predicate, so every test still passes if `nativeHistoryBlocked` is removed from `centerExtensions` or loses its precedence over history()'s beforeinput handler. The fix is not proven to be wired into the middle pane, which open_risks also says.
fix: Add a WebKit test (`editor/*.browser.test.ts`). It builds a center pane, types a character, dispatches a cancelable `new InputEvent("beforeinput", { inputType: "historyUndo" })` on its contentDOM, and expects the text to be unchanged and the event to be defaultPrevented.

problem: #699 The preferenceEffects tests catch a missing theme, find-key or kind-key effect, but nothing tests `setPreferences` or the `sideRunner` lookup. A loop that skipped the right pane, gave a side the "center" effects, or a `sideRunner` combine that returned null would pass every test: pane.test.ts:430 checks only that a binding for "a" exists, not that pressing it reaches `#focus.run`.
fix: Add a WebKit controller test. Build a MergeController, call `setPreferences` with apply bound to "a", focus a change in the right pane, press "a", and expect the summary to drop by one.

problem: #700 `problemKey` leaves out the path. A Move (or a recorded location changed elsewhere) to a file with the same broken keys therefore keeps the shown Keys problem, and its text (problemText.ts:100) still names the old path.
fix: Count the key problems as changed when `read.path` differs from `before.read?.path`, e.g. by passing the old path into the `sameProblems` check.

problem: #701 `return run !== null` suggests a pane without a runner leaves the key alone, as the report claims. With `preventDefault: true`, CodeMirror still prevents the key (@codemirror/view runHandlers: `if (binding.preventDefault) prevented = true`), so the null branch changes nothing a user sees.
fix: Give the facet a no-op default and always return true. Or set preventDefault only when a runner exists, and correct the report's claim.

problem: #702 'Add Keyboard Shortcut' opens the dialog empty, but WebStorm's ShortcutDialog.showAndGet (ShortcutDialog.java:108-112) fills it with the action's first key when no key is selected. The implementer chose this deviation on their own, not the owner.
fix: Either pass the action's first key as the dialog's `initial` while keeping `from: null` (WebStorm's behaviour), or raise 'Add opens empty vs prefilled' as a product question for the owner and record the answer before landing.

problem: #703 `owners` re-implements 'which other action already holds this key' (KEY_ACTIONS filter + sameKey), which keymapEdit.ts `placed` (line 47) already decides for the clash question. A later change to the clash rule would update the question but not the live warning.
fix: Export one `keyOwners(bindings, action, key)` from keymapEdit.ts, use it in `placed` and in KeyRecorder, and report this as a needed change to the read-only keymapEdit.ts.

problem: #704 `plusMenuKey` (KeyRecorder:108-123) and `menuKey` (KeymapList:92-106) are the same Escape/Tab-close plus wrap-around Up/Down menu handler, with two identical step tables (MENU_STEPS:21, ROW_STEPS:19). The two menus' keyboard rules will drift.
fix: Move one step table and one pure `stepMenuItem(menu: HTMLElement, event: KeyboardEvent): void` into a single ui module used by both handlers (and list it in the project map).

problem: #705 'board item 662' (and 'board item 690' at editor/internal/pane.ts:182) is a new reference form chosen to dodge palette.ts HEX_COLOUR. The house form for a decision is `plan §2 #NN` (MergeView.vue:140), and architecture.md:621 already cites #57 for this constant. #690 is a review-finding id, which is change history, not a source.
fix: Write '(plan §2 #57)' in MergeToolbar. In pane.ts, drop 'board item 690' and keep only the @codemirror/commands citation, and change 'only yamt's keys and toolbar undo' to 'only yamt's undo commands undo', since the toolbar buttons are now hidden.

problem: #706 SET_KEYS silently drops a text that does not parse (flatMap → []). ipc/keys.ts already builds its constant keys by throwing on a bad literal (`defaultKeys`, keys.ts:195-199), so this adds a second convention that hides a typo as a missing menu entry.
fix: Throw on a null parse as `defaultKeys` does, or ask for ipc/keys.ts (the one source of what keys mean) to export the four ShortcutTextField keys.

problem: #707 The map (and docs/architecture.md:646) still describes keyText.ts as 'action names, places, groups'. It now also owns the edit menu's entries and rules (keymapMenu with isDefault), the + menu (setKeyMenu) and the conflict line (usedByText), so a reader looking for the menu rules will not find them through the map.
fix: Extend both entries as the implementer suggested: 'keyText.ts (action names, places, groups; the Keymap edit menu `keymapMenu`, the + menu `setKeyMenu`, the conflict line `usedByText`)'.

problem: #708 `useDefault` is a plain click handler but carries the `use*` prefix the house reserves for composables.
fix: Rename it to `moveToDefault` (and update the template's @click).

problem: #709 `SetKeyEntry` is exported but nothing imports it; it only types setKeyMenu's return in the same file.
fix: Drop the `export` keyword.

problem: #710 A click outside an open menu always moves focus back to the row, even when the click lands on a focusable control. The onClickOutside handler runs in the capture phase, then closeMenu focuses the row after nextTick. So clicking into the Settings file field while a menu is open puts focus back on the row: typed characters are lost, and Space/Enter reopens the menu.
fix: In the click-outside handler, close the menu and refocus the row only when focus did not move to another element (document.activeElement is body or still inside the menu); Escape and Tab keep the current refocus.

problem: #711 The dialog's key rules have no automated test; only the manual WebKit pass checks them. A regression would still pass `pnpm test`, for example Shift+Tab being recorded, Enter confirming an empty field, Escape with Shift cancelling, or `owners` counting the action's own keys.
fix: Move the field's decision (cancel | confirm | leave | record key | ignore, given the event and the shown key) and the owners filter into a pure function in a ui/*.ts module, and give it a node test next to keyText.test.ts.

problem: #712 `index < entries.length - 1` can never be false: a trailing separator needs an action with no keys whose defaults are also empty, and no entry in DEFAULT_KEYS is empty. So this is a condition no test can reach, and a mutant removing it would survive.
fix: Drop the trailing-separator clause and keep only the doubled-separator check, or cite in the comment the real case that reaches it.

problem: #713 The stored WebKit evidence is cut off at 768 characters ('…'). The record therefore does not show two acceptance items: Find emptied then Add opening empty with OK disabled, and a click into the Settings file field keeping focus and taking typed text. Only the open_risks prose says the field kept focus.

problem: #714 (same as previous) The committed report's WebKit `observed` line is cut at 768 characters (line 105 says "[Some lines truncated to 768 chars]"). The pasted evidence for these Acceptance items is missing from the record: OK changes nothing, Find emptied then Add opens empty with OK disabled, the Settings file field keeps focus and takes typed text, and the + menu's Escape/Tab.

problem: #715 `FieldKey` (keyField.ts:3) and `MenuStep` (menuKeys.ts:3) are exported but nothing imports them; each only types its own function's return value. This is the same pattern #709 removed from keyText.ts in this rework, and knip does not catch it.

problem: #716 The cancel/confirm tests change only Shift, and the Tab test changes only Ctrl. A regression to `plain = !event.shiftKey`, or dropping `altKey` from `modified`, passes all four tests, while Ctrl+Escape would then close the dialog instead of being recorded and Ctrl+Enter would confirm.

#753 start.ts has two jobs. It holds start-app's own steps (Xvfb, tauri-driver, recording) and also the session lifecycle that start-fixture shares: `tempFolder` (line 36), `launchTracked` (91), `withCleanup` (100), `Save` (24), `DRIVER_READY_MS` (33). So fixture.ts:4 imports from another command's module. The next start-* command or lifecycle rule will land in start-app's file, which turns it into the god module of the tool.
fix: Move tempFolder, launchTracked, withCleanup, Save and DRIVER_READY_MS into one session-lifecycle module (session.ts is the natural owner), imported by start.ts, fixture.ts and focus.ts, so start.ts keeps only startApp's steps.
triage: block (growth: start.ts takes the shared lifecycle)

problem: #754 focus.ts writes the state file itself (lines 36 and 51) and makes its own spawn-then-record step (`launch` + `writeState` with the proc appended). It also recomputes the logs folder as `join(app.folder, "logs")` (line 33), next to start.ts:41. The rule "every spawned process is recorded in the state file at once" and the logs location now have two copies, so the state file has two write paths. A change to how processes are tracked (the safety guarantee `stop` relies on) must be made twice, or focus-away silently diverges.
fix: Have focus-away/focus-back go through the shared lifecycle module: launchTracked with a save that writes the state, plus a matching untrack/save for focus-back. Derive the logs folder from `state.folder` in one exported function there, which also removes the `logDir` parameter threaded through appSteps/startDisplay/startDriver/recordingLaunch/finishRecording and fixtureSteps.
triage: block (growth: a second write path for the state file)

problem: #755 session.ts mixes three concepts: repo-root path resolution (`fromRoot`), X display environment (`displayEnv`) and state lookup (`sessionNamed`/`appSession`). Meanwhile the name → state-file step `readState(statePath(name))` is recomposed at start.ts:37, stop.ts:43 and session.ts:19. As the tool grows this file becomes the place for every next shared helper (a utils.ts by another name), and readers cannot tell which module owns session lookup.
fix: Make session.ts the session-lifecycle module (lookup, plus the helpers from the start.ts finding) with one `sessionNamed`/`findSession(name)` used by start, stop and the drive commands. Move displayEnv to processes.ts (process environment) and fromRoot to its own small `root.ts`.
triage: promoted: session.ts becoming a catch-all module

problem: #760 Survivor colours.ts:82:38: framesWithMatch with `> 0` flipped to `<= 0` still passes, because every column of the test data has 2 matching and 2 non-matching frames. If that number ever inverts, a recording whose every frame is dark would read as 'no dark frame'. That number is the per-hex verdict the brief defines and checkers use to judge a flash.
fix: Use asymmetric data, e.g. [[0],[0],[3]] gives 1 and [[1],[1],[0]] gives 2, so an inverted or >= predicate fails.

problem: #761 Survivor colours.ts:72:35: collapseRows with `every` replaced by `some` still passes, because each row change in the test changes every column at once. With the acceptance run's 3 colours, a frame range where only the dark column changes would merge into its neighbour, and the table would hide the flash it exists to show.
fix: Add rows that differ in one column only, e.g. collapseRows([[0,5],[1,5]]) gives two rows.

problem: #762 Survivors colours.ts:27:10 and 54:20: the frame-boundary tests take their frame size from frameBytes(2, 1) and frameBytes(1, 1), so a frameBytes that drops the height, or divides by it, still passes. A pixel loop that reads 2 pixels past the frame end (masked by `?? 0`) also passes, because no test counts 000000. video.ts sizes every decoded frame from frameBytes, and the brief names 'colour off-by-one at frame boundaries' as a bug the tests must catch.
fix: Assert frameBytes(1600, 1000) === 4_800_000 (or use a 2x2 frame in the split test), and assert countColours over one frame with no black pixels for colour 000000 gives [0].
triage: block: frame-size/boundary rule untested

fix: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(<one const>)` to fetch in webdriver(), so endSession reports 'not ended: …' and stop still kills the process groups.

problem: #836 In the middle pane, pressing Delete with the cursor at a wave's `from`, or Backspace at its `to`, deletes every hidden line of that run with one key. The cursor starts there: the middle's first cursor is at 0, which is run 0's `from` (implementer's open_risks). It also lands there after ArrowDown or ArrowUp onto a wave (acceptance 5). Plan #63 has edits at a hidden edge show only that line, as typing does. [INFERENCE] WebStorm deletes one character at a collapsed fold's edge and expands the fold; it does not delete the region.
fix: In `folds.ts`, add a middle-pane `EditorState.transactionFilter` that turns any `delete.*` user event from an empty cursor that removes a displayed hidden range whole (Delete at `from`, Backspace at `to`, including the group and line-end variants) into that run's `showFolds` with no text change. Prove it with a state test: a `delete.forward` transaction over `[from, to]` from a cursor at `from` leaves the text unchanged and drops the run's outer level.

The rework, which is rewiring `index.ts`'s fold code, can take this.

problem: #861 Acceptance 2 allows at most 1 device px where the wave meets each edge, but the report measures C|remote at 1.18–1.29 (ratio 2, 1237 px, file list hidden) and 1.04 (ratio 1, 1600 px, hidden). problem: #862 The mask draws one wave every `round(64·P, 1px)/64` px, not the `period` P that `wavePhase` computed and its 1e-9 node tests check. The middle's right edge is therefore off by up to (k+½)/128 CSS px (≈0.2 px for a 500 px middle, ≈0.46 px for 1200 px), and nothing tests it. The period is now decided in two places: connectors works it out exactly, and a CSS expression changes it afterwards. That error grows as the window gets wider.

triage: promoted: the period decided in two places (connectors exact, CSS rounding after) with an untested error growing with width — growth harm; fixed with the block

Anyone later tuning the mask for Chromium/WebView2 at 1.25 will read the comment as a contradiction.
