problem: #866 The middle pane's phase is pinned for the period `P = D/(k+½)` (`connectors/index.ts:64`), but the mask draws a different period, `round(64·P)/64`. The difference builds up over the stretch and appears only at the middle's right edge (C|remote): `(k+½)·|64P − round(64P)|/64`, up to `(k+½)/128` CSS px. I recomputed it from the implementer's recorded layouts: +0.155 CSS px in `d1-1600-nolist` (≈0.19 px vertical at slope 1.2), the layout measured at 1.04, and +0.100 CSS px in `d2-1237-nolist` (≈0.24 device px), the layout measured at 1.18. So the two failing cases are both on the one edge this rounding moves. Two modules now decide the drawn period, and the node tests use the unrounded one, so they cannot see the gap.
fix: Decide the drawn period once in `connectors`: move `MASK_PERIODS` next to `wavePhase` and have the `through` case return `round(64·P)/64` as its period. Pin the offset at the midpoint of `enters` and `leaves`, so each edge gets at most half the remaining drift. Extend the `through` sweep to check that both edges are met within `(k+½)/256` px using the returned period. `foldView` then multiplies `var(period)` by 64 without a second rounding rule.
triage: promoted: block — same cause as #861/#862; round 2 decides the drawn period once in `connectors` (rounded so 64 waves are whole CSS px), pins the middle at its midpoint, tests both edges with the returned period

problem: #867 The acceptance limit is 1 device px. These layouts miss it: WebKit C|remote is 1.04 (ratio 1, 1600, file list hidden) and 1.18–1.29 (ratio 2, 1237, file list hidden); Chromium at ratio 1.25 has L|local at 1.11–1.13. The owner asked for the wave to be consistent across devices, and the implementer's own probe shows that edges snapped to device pixels bring the worst case down to 0.77–0.86. As committed, a step above 1 px is still visible at some window widths.
fix: After the first fix, measure C|remote again in the two failing WebKit layouts. If it is still over 1 device px, round the measured edges to device pixels in `#measure` (`Math.round(x·devicePixelRatio)/devicePixelRatio`, as in the probe) and measure again on a `matchMedia('(resolution: …dppx)')` change. If neither is done, the owner has to relax the 1 device px line in the brief explicitly.
triage: promoted: block — round 2 re-measures; WebKit at ratios 1 and 2 (engine of record; GTK draws only whole ratios, plan §3) must meet ≤ 1 device px, snapping the measured edges to device pixels (re-measured on a resolution change) if needed; Chromium at 1.25/1.5 (WebView2 stand-in) is held to ≤ 1.5 device px because it snaps the mask's position to device pixels while the joins are anti-aliased at sub-pixel y — recorded in #64

problem: #877 Reset has to ask `at_open` two questions that must agree: `regular_entry()` picks the entry (writes.rs:108), and `seen_after_reset(disk)` picks the view (writes.rs:131-134). The second one takes back a clone of the payload `at_open` already holds, and its `AtOpen::Unread` arm can never run, because `regular_entry` returns `None` for `Unread`. Growth: a new `AtOpen` variant or a new reset rule has to be decided in both methods and kept consistent by hand. The types allow a `Seen` for an `Unread` reset even though that state cannot happen.
fix: Replace both methods with one, e.g. `AtOpen::reset_to(&self) -> Option<(OnDisk, Seen)>` (or a small `ResetTo { entry, seen }`) that returns the entry and the view from the same match. `reset` then writes `entry` and assigns `seen` with no second lookup.
triage: promoted: one reset decision split across two AtOpen methods that must agree (copied decision)

problem: #878 `open_file` first builds every readable file as `AtOpen::Untouched` with `Seen::ViewFromStages`. After `check.untouched`, `changed_at_open` rewrites both fields. So the rule 'Changed/Unread → `Seen::GitOutput`' is written twice (open.rs:128-131 and 75-85), and the `AtOpen::Changed(_)` arm in `file_state` never runs. Growth: the next fact derived from the at-open state has to be patched in both places, and `FileState.at_open` ('Set once by `open`') is in fact assigned twice.
fix: Have `open_file` return the parts, the `OnDisk` and the `StartLook`, and build each `FileState` once after `check.untouched` with the final `AtOpen`. Derive `seen` from it in one place, e.g. an `AtOpen::first_seen()` in disk.rs.
triage: promoted: the at-open -> seen rule written twice and at_open assigned twice (two writers)

problem: #879 Whether a block is exact is branched on twice. `seed` picks `waiting` from `located.exact` (lines 53-58), and `push_conflict` separately picks base lines or disk lines from `located.exact` (lines 104-108). The result goes into a third parallel `Vec` (`waiting`), which `seeded` zips by position with `chunks` and `ranges`. Growth: each new per-chunk fact adds another parallel vector and another copy of the exact/inexact branch. Nothing user-visible changes today.
fix: Pass `Option<&Block>` to `push_conflict` (`None` for a raw region) so its one `if located.exact` branch pushes the base lines plus `block_markers`, or the disk lines plus `Waiting::AsShown`. Keep each chunk's range and waiting together in one `Vec<(LineRange<MiddleLine>, Waiting)>`.
triage: promoted: exactness branched twice and a third parallel per-chunk vector (copied decision, grows per fact)

problem: #883 Survivor `rebuild_markers -> Ok(())` is not equivalent and can hide a bug users would see. Take Remote on the symlink conflict, then Reset: with the mutant, git lists the file as conflicted again, but the worktree link still points at `remote-target`. That is the taken side, not what Reset promises. The same gap covers a regular file that was unreadable at open. The patch moved RK17's proving test (`reset_after_finish_restores_git_stages_and_conflict_markers`) onto the at-open-bytes path, so #69's rule (links, submodules and unread files keep `checkout -m`) has no test that runs `checkout -m`. `reset_after_take_brings_back_the_stages_of_every_kind` includes SYMLINK but only checks `ls-files -u`.

L
R
>>>>>>> theirs

problem: #892 A server's run phase is stored in six places that must change together: `Server.#state`, `#attempt` and `#halting` (server.ts:43-45), plus `Attempt.run`, `hasExited`, `docs` and `folder` (attempt.ts:11-14, public and mutable, `docs`/`folder` written by server.ts:133,185). rule_id: R-lsp-9 (brief rule 2, rule 9: stop keeps it stopped; no leaked run)
problem: #900 While a server is `stopping`, `start()` or `restart()` queues `#halting.then(() => this.#startWhenIdle())`, and that callback launches a new run without checking whether anything later cancelled it. Three cases follow. (a) Restart and then Stop inside the shutdown window (up to 2 s shutdown + 2 s host kill): the server ends up `running` with `userStopped` true, so the user's Stop is ignored. (b) A `setSpecs` that drops or changes the spec in that window: the retired `Server` still launches, which leaks a process nobody stops. That process opens every served document and keeps calling `showProblems` under the same server name as the replacement, so the editor's single slot for that name gets problems from an old spec's run. (c) `destroy()` in that window resolves first (the queued callback is registered before destroy's `Promise.all`), and the run starts after destroy.
fix: Track whether a start is still wanted (e.g. a `#wantsStart` flag set by `start`/`restart`, cleared by `halt()` before `restart` sets it again). The deferred callback launches only if the flag is still set. Add tests: restart then stop with `ignoresStop`, restart then `setSpecs([])`, and restart then `destroy()`; each should end with `host.servers` unchanged and the state `stopped`.
triage: block

rule_id: R-lsp-9 (brief rule 9/10: stop ordering, log words)
problem: #901 `#exited` closes the connection only for the current attempt. If a run exits while `#release` waits on `shutdown`, the request is not ended: the stop stays `stopping` for the full 2 s, then logs the false line 'No answer to shutdown within 2 s; cancelled' after 'Exited with code 0', and sends `$/cancelRequest` and `exit` to a run that is already gone. The test `rule 9: a server that exits during shutdown is not stopped again` (index.test.ts:1669) advances 2000 ms, so it locks in this delay instead of catching it.
fix: In `#exited`, call `attempt.connection.close()` for every attempt, not only the current one, so the pending shutdown settles `closed` at once. Change the test to `settle()` without advancing 2 s, and assert the state is `stopped`, there is no 'No answer to shutdown within' line, and no `exit` or `$/cancelRequest` was sent after the exit.
triage: block

problem: #910 Nothing tests the output drain, so the `Exited comes once, last` contract (in the HostEvent doc and in bindings.ts) and its 1 s cap are unproven. Survivors 191:34 (`+`→`-`), 192:11 (delete `!`) and 192:74 (`==`/`>`) remove the drain, so `Log`/`Message` can arrive after `Exited`; the window then logs a crashed server's last stderr lines after "Exited with code N". Survivor 192:56 (`&&`→`||`) turns the cap into an endless wait whenever a grandchild still holds the pipes: `Exited` is never sent and `stop_all` never returns, so the app hangs on close. The poll this relies on (the implementer's deviation 'a server that exits while something else holds its stdout still produces Exited') is also untested.

problem: #913 Behaviour 2 says a reloaded page's runs stop themselves, but they do not. Tauri 2.12.1's `Channel::send` only fails when `webview.eval` fails (implementer's open risk; confirmed in ipc/channel.rs:413-449), and nothing in the app prevents reload: F5/Ctrl+R are not blocked in src-tauri or ui. triage: block

problem: #914 `read_log` returns `OutputClosed` at stderr EOF or on a read error, and that stops the whole run. A server that closes or redirects its stderr while still serving over stdout is therefore killed, although only stdout EOF (or the child's exit, already polled) means the server is gone. Nothing gets harder as the app grows beyond this case.

problem: #917 Three of the six #897 survivors can be seen through the public API, so the #916 triage ('memory only, not observable') is wrong for them. The other three (empty block, `this.#retired`, `=> true`) stay as equivalent: they keep a halted server, and halting an idle server resolves at once.

problem: #922 A pure line diff turns a reindent into one edit that replaces every changed line, so an edit that reaches past an open block's edge breaks the block. If it covers the block and the line after it (for example a formatter reindenting a function around the block), both `from` and `to` are strictly inside the replaced range. `mapPos(-1)` maps both to the edit's start, the span collapses, and `chunkField` marks the block `ignored ignored` with no arrows, although every line of the block is still there. If the edit covers only line 199 and the block's first line, `from` moves to line 199, so the block grows, and applying a side then deletes line 199 from the Result. The node check `mapPos` of a span [12,21) through a reindent of lines 3–9 gave [6,6]. The acceptance test changes only lines 3 and 400, far from the block, so it cannot catch this.
fix: Inside each `LineEdit`, pair old and new lines one to one. Replace each pair on its own, trimmed to the characters that differ, and insert or delete only the extra lines, so no single change straddles a line edge. Add a test that reindents lines 198–204 around the block and expects `pending pending`, the block's own text and the `replace` arrows. Optional: the same change keeps problems on reformatted lines (open risk 1).
triage: block

fix: Split the result on any line break (`Text.of(reply.result.split(/\r\n?|\n/))`, CodeMirror's default split) so the Result keeps its own separator. problem: #924 Every server answer dispatches `setDiagnostics`, even when the merged list is exactly what is already shown. problem: #926 `servers::manage` builds `HostState` and also registers the app's page-load hook, so a function named for managed state now holds a hook Tauri keeps only one of: `Builder::on_page_load` replaces any earlier hook (tauri-2.12.1 app.rs:1854 `self.on_page_load.replace(..)`). problem: #927 `typedWhileAllWait` decides on its own which Result text Save drops (`AsShown`, or no changed side decided, via `sideChanged`). `fileText.ts:24` `writtenLines` makes the same decision with a different formula (`isResolved`, then per kind; a half-decided `Markers` keeps the shown lines). The two agree today only because `status.ts` `markConflictSideOrChange` moves both changed sides of a non-conflict together. The dot is defined as "typing that is not written" (brief behaviour 4, plan #69). So any change to the write rules (design open question 1 (b), or a new `Waiting` kind) can clear the dot while the typing is still left out of the file. problem: #936 A common case breaks: the user resolves a conflict by typing into the Result while both sides are still waiting, then clicks Mark resolved. `finish` writes `asShown()` (the typing included) and stages it. But `markSaved` re-checks `typedWhileAllWait`, which still returns true, so the dot stays on for good. The close question then lists a file that is fully written and staged, and Ctrl+S cannot clear the dot (a resolved file saves `asShown`, nothing changes). The same happens for any file git already lists as Resolved.

Add a savedPoint test: type inside a fully waiting conflict, mark saved as asShown, and the dot clears.
triage: block

L
z
" with local applied, delete the break after "L" → span [2,3), `spanLines` = ["Lz"], so the file becomes "a
<<<<<<< ours
Lz
=======
R1
R2
>>>>>>> theirs
z
" with "z" twice. Deleting the break before "L" writes "a" twice the same way. The edge-break test only covers a conflict with both sides waiting, where `spanLines` is never called.

problem: #940 Surviving mutant: `target.writing.add(path)` removed in `whileWriting`, so reset and finish no longer claim the path. The test "a save while a %s of the same file runs is ignored" (store.test.ts:2495) checks only the final `saves` list. That list is the same whether the save was ignored during the reset and sent afterwards, or sent during the reset and skipped afterwards. This test is the only evidence for "finish and reset register in it too" (Behaviour 2), and it passes with that registration deleted. Without the claim, a Save can overwrite Reset's restored bytes: Rust's reset leaves the disk version as it is (writes.rs:102-131).

problem: #941 Surviving mutants: `.some` → `.every` (line 90) and `file.path === path` → `true` (line 91). The resolved test (store.test.ts:2381) lists only a.ts. Under the second mutant, any resolved file elsewhere in the list makes an unresolved file write `asShown()`: its waiting conflicts go to disk as base text without markers, and the next start stages it. That is exactly the silent loss of a side that plan #65 rules out. Under `.every`, a resolved file in a list of several writes `fileText()` and puts markers back into it.

problem: #942 Deviation 2 lets Reset run while an earlier Save still holds the claim. The window is the Save's wait on `handle.format()`: Reset can write the at-open bytes and start its reload, and then the Save resumes. `handle.snapshot()` still returns the old controller, so the Save sends the pre-reset text with a disk version Rust still accepts, because reset does not change it. The disk ends up undoing the Reset while the view reloads to the reset content with no dot. This is exactly what the design's claim was meant to prevent ("Save cannot slip between Reset's reply and its reload"). It is unreachable today only because MergeView passes `servers: null`, so `format()` returns at once. The status-area slice that wires servers will make it reachable without touching this file.
fix: Make the claim exclusive both ways: reset and finish wait for, or refuse during, a save's claim. Or let save drop its write when another write to the path started during `format()` (for example a per-path counter that reset and finish increase, checked before `snapshot()`). Add a store test where format is still pending while a reset completes.
triage: block

problem:
#945 #922 is fixed only when an edit keeps the same number of lines. When a formatter splits or joins a line next to an open block and also changes the block's first line, lineDiff gives one LineEdit. `lineChanges` then pairs its lines by position, so text moves across the block's edge. A probe ran the real `formatResult` and `chunkField` (tsx, read-only). (B) Old `function f(a,` / `b) {` / one-line block `B1` / `}`, formatted to `function f(a, b) {` / `  B1` / `}`: the block becomes `ignored ignored` with no arrows, even though `  B1` is still in the Result. This is the exact symptom #922 reported. (A) Old `foo(x, y)` / `B1` / `B2`, formatted to `foo(x,` / `  y)` / `  B1` / `B2`: the block becomes `"  y)
  B1
B2
"`, so applying a side deletes `  y)` from the Result. (B2) With a two-line block the block loses its first line. (C, open risk 1) A blank line the formatter adds after a reindented last block line joins the block. The added tests only cover reindents that keep the line count. Each would still pass if pairing across block edges were wrong, so none of them catches this.
fix: Inside each LineEdit, pair lines with a second `lineDiff` on whitespace-free keys (`line.replace(/\s+/g, "")`). Reindented lines then always pair with themselves, and positional pairing and the extra-line insert or delete happen only in the sub-edits left unmatched. An extra line with no pair goes at the start of the next line, as it does today. Add format tests for (A) split before the block and (B) a join before a one-line block: `pending pending`, the block's own text, and `replace` arrows.
triage: block: editor fix round 2 (last)

problem: #946 The new `root` parameter makes detection compute the project's workspace URI (`fileUri(root, folder)`) a second time, and oxlint needs it to match the URI `handshake.ts` `projectFolder(spec, root).uri` sends; `specOf(preset, detected, folder, root)` and `detectIn(lookups, folder, root)` also take two plain strings that can be swapped without a type error. Growth question: if the handshake ever changes how it builds that URI (separators, drive letter, trailing slash), oxlint quietly stops applying `run: "onType"`, and every caller of `detect` has to fetch `root` before it can call it.
fix: Pass the preset's `initializationOptions` function (workspaceUri → options) through to the spec and call it in `initializeParams` with `folder.uri`, then drop `root` from `detect`, `detectIn` and `specOf`. This is the brief's 'build it at start' option and needs `handshake.ts`/`spec.ts` in a fix round. If the parameter stays, at least pass `{ folder, root }` as an object to `specOf`/`detectIn`.
triage: promoted: the project folder's URI built in two places (detection and the handshake); a change to one silently breaks oxlint's onType

problem: #947 The native preview counts as installed when `node_modules/@typescript/native-preview/package.json` exists, so detection has a second test for 'the project has this program' next to `findProgram(...).place === "Project"`, which oxfmt and oxlint use and which starting `tsgo` also uses. A detected `tsgo` with `install: null` can therefore still fail to start with NotFound, against design §1 ('detected and can start never disagree'). Growth question: whoever adds the next preset has two rules to choose from, and the status area's 'not installed' versus 'not found' depends on which one was picked.
fix: Decide the native preview with `findProgram(project, look.nativePreview.command.program)` and `found.kind === "Found" && found.place === "Project"`, the same way as `projectProgram`. Drop `nativePreview.package` from `presets.ts` and from `lookedFor`.
triage: promoted: a second 'the project has this program' rule; detected and can-start may disagree

problem: #951 #945 is fixed only when the block's edge line changes in whitespace alone. If the formatter also changes a token on that line, a split or join next to the block still leaves the whole edit unmatched. `lineChanges` then pairs it by position, and all three symptoms of #945 come back. (B) `line 198`/`line 199`/one-line block `block 1` formatted to `line 198 line 199`/`  block 1;` gives keys `line198,line199,block1` against `line198line199,block1;`. Nothing matches, so line 199 gets `  block 1;` and line 200 is deleted, which is the whole block. The block becomes `ignored ignored` with no arrows, although its text is still in the Result. This is the `function f(a,`/`b) {`/`return 'x'` → `function f(a, b) {`/`  return "x";` case, where quotes and semicolons change. (A) `foo(x, y)`/`B1` formatted to `foo(x,`/`  y)`/`  B1;` puts `  y)` inside the block. (C) a reindented last line that gains a `;` plus a blank line after it inserts the blank at that line's end, inside the block. #945's Problem says 'changes the block's first line', not 'reindents' it. The four new tests (format.test.ts:253-300) use only whitespace changes on the edge line, so they pass while these cases still break.
fix: Pair the lines of each unmatched sub-edit by similarity of their whitespace-free keys before falling back to position, for example the Dice ≥ 50 % pairing of plan §2 #31 / merge-core `line_pairs`. Unpaired lines are then inserted or deleted next to their neighbours rather than moved across the edge. Add (A), (B), (B2) and (C) variants in which the edge line also gains a `;` or a quote change, each asserting `pending pending`, the block's own text, `replace` arrows and one undo step.
triage: block: beyond two rounds → Gate B; decided by the orchestrator as owner (#876): a third round with a product rule (#952)

problem: #953 Surviving mutant `typeof value === "string"` → true. Brief Behaviour 4 says a malformed package.json counts as "no field / no version", and no test checks that for a non-string value. With the mutant, `{"version": 7}` in node_modules/typescript/package.json detects `tsc`, a numeric 5 reaches `InstallHint.reason.version`, which is typed `string`, and `{"packageManager": ["pnpm@9"]}` becomes pnpm because the regex turns the array into a string. The test at detect.test.ts:397 (`{"packageManager":3}`) passes either way, because "3" never matches the regex. What gets harder: every later reader of `jsonField` can count on a string that no test protects.
fix: In the "not detected … with no version" test (detect.test.ts:276), add a tree whose typescript package.json is `{"version":7}` and expect `[]`. In the field test, change the `3` case to `{"packageManager":["pnpm@9"]}` with an `app/yarn.lock` and expect "yarn".
triage: promoted: the string guard on package.json fields is a rule other code relies on, untested

problem: #954 Surviving mutants `^\d+` → `^\d` and → `\d+`. Every test version has a one-digit major and starts with a digit, so nothing pins how the major is read. With `^\d`, a TypeScript 10.0.0 project reads as major 1 and is told to install typescript-language-server ("needs the separate package"). With the unanchored form, a version such as "x7.0.0" is detected as TS 7 even though Behaviour 4 says it has no version. What gets harder: the TS ≥ 7 split is the whole choice of TypeScript server, and its parse has no test.
fix: Add two cases: `typescriptAt("", "10.0.0")` must give `TypeScript tsc --lsp --stdio @` (kills `^\d`), and a version of "x7.0.0" must give `[]` in the not-detected loop (kills `\d+`).
triage: promoted: the TypeScript major parse decides the server and has no test (TS 10 would read as 1)

problem: #955 The implementer's own rule ("an empty command is skipped: there is no program to name or start") only covers `[]`. A command of `[""]` (for example a Command field with a leading space split on spaces, design §8) or a program like `"bin/"` still gives a spec named "" (then " (2)") whose program cannot start. What gets harder: the Settings slice has to remember to trim before calling `addedSpecs`, which is a second copy of this rule.
fix: Skip the entry when the program's file name `base` is "" (one condition replacing `program === undefined`), and add `{ command: [""] }` and `{ command: ["bin/"] }` to the "empty command is skipped" test.

If lsp's rule ever changes (for example, counts while `starting`), the ui guard will quietly override it. Growth: a second place decides when a file counts as served.

problem: #960 `Screen` is the window's navigation type, and the store creates its ref (store.ts:101). It is defined in servers.ts, while writes to `screen` are split between store.ts (`pick`, `openSettings`, `closeSettings`) and servers.ts (`showServerLog`, `closeServerLog`). `shownLog` is refreshed only by servers.ts's writes, so the store's writes leave it stale. Growth: the next screen kind (the setup question or a settings section) has to be added in the servers module, and finding "what can change `screen`" takes two files.

problem: #963 Behaviour 5 says the log stays put when the user has scrolled up. That breaks once a server's log reaches `LogBook`'s 2000-line cap (`lsp/internal/log.ts` `LOG_LINES`): each new line drops the first one. The rows are keyed by `index`, so Vue rewrites every row's text in place while `scrollTop` stays the same. The text the user is reading then moves up one row for every stderr or `window/logMessage` line. A busy server such as typescript-language-server reaches the cap in one session. No test covers following the end or staying put. The report's open_risks says neither was exercised live.
fix: Key each row by a stable identity (lines dropped so far + index, or a WeakMap id per `LogLine` object). While `following` is false, record the top visible row and its offset in a `flush: "pre"` watch and put it back in the `flush: "post"` watch. Put the 'how many lines were dropped above' rule in a pure helper (find the old first `LogLine` by identity in the new array) and give it a node test that covers the cap.
triage: block

problem: #964 `serverViews.value.some(running)` is there only so that a `computed` re-runs on `onChange`, because `servers.serving` is not reactive. It looks like a second condition, though. As more servers are added, someone may 'simplify' this clause and quietly break when the counts appear.

Add a case where `computed(() => slice.serving(path))` turns true after Start (this kills dropping the reactive read). Make the read's purpose plain, e.g. a one-line comment that it subscribes to `onChange`.
triage: promoted: same clause as #957; the tests that pin the reactive read and the any-running rule go with its fix

problem: #966 Escape now runs through `serverSetup.dismissQuestion` for every question, including exit, clash and unprocessed (App.vue:101 → QuestionDialog `dismiss`). serverSetup works out that a question was dismissed by comparing a `dismissals` counter before and after an `await` (:91-96). It also copies asking's one-question-at-a-time rule (:88 repeats asking.ts:19), because asking's `false` cannot be told apart from Don't start. So the waiting question is ended by two modules, and the dialog's general behaviour is tested in serverSetup.test.ts:330 ('Escape on another question still means its cancel'). Growth: the next question that has to tell Escape apart from No must either go through the language-server module or add another counter, and asking.ts no longer owns how its questions end.
fix: Have asking.ts answer with three outcomes, for example `ask` resolving to `"yes" | "no" | "dismissed"` plus a `dismiss()` (existing callers map `"yes"` to true). Wire `dismissQuestion: asking.dismiss` in store.ts and delete `dismissals`, the `question.value !== null` pre-check and the dismissal tests from serverSetup. The orchestrator has to grant asking.ts, which is outside `Owned`.
triage: block

problem: #967 `projectLabel` copies how a project folder reads, which serverText.ts:147 (`installText`) already decides ("" → the repository root, otherwise `folder/`). Settings now takes this server label from the question-words module (LanguageServerSettings.vue:7,64). The words for a server that is not installed now exist three times: question.ts:36 "(not installed)", LanguageServerSettings.vue:32 "not installed", and serverText.ts:81 "Not installed". The map puts every server word in serverText.ts. Growth: changing how a folder or a missing server reads means finding and editing two or three modules, and they will drift apart.
fix: Move `projectLabel` and one not-installed label into serverText.ts. Use `projectLabel` inside `installText`'s folder line. Have question.ts `serversText` and LanguageServerSettings.vue import both from serverText.ts.

problem: #968 Three places each own a piece of the start and focus flow. The rule 'detect after the file list and the settings are in' is written once for start in main.ts:16 and again for focus as `await Promise.all(...)` then `findServers()` in App.vue:44-49. serverSetup.ts:112/116 adds a `started` guard on top. App.vue is supposed to be a composition surface with no feature logic. Growth: a new input to detection has to be awaited in both main.ts and App.vue, and App.vue keeps picking up flow logic.
fix: Give serverSetup's target `loadFiles`, `refreshFiles` and `loadSettings`, and expose `start()` and `refocus()` that do the ordering themselves. main.ts calls `store.start()` and App.vue's watch calls `refocus()`, so the ordering and the `started` guard live in one module.

problem: #969 Don't start stops the running servers by calling `setSpecs([])` first. That only works because of how the private `LanguageServers.#create` carries `userStopped` across a reconcile, and the comment quotes that private member. lsp offers no named operation to stop servers without marking them as stopped by the user. Growth: a refactor of lsp's private carry-over silently changes Don't start, and the next caller that needs the same thing has to copy the two-call trick.
fix: Have lsp provide the behaviour, for example `setSpecs(specs, { startOnOpen: false })` halting live runs without `userStopped`, or a `halt()` (needs a grant, lsp is read-only here). Then `answer` calls only `apply`, and the comment goes.

problem: #973 `answer()` applies the new choice even when `setServerAnswer` fails. Failures are real here: a broken or unwritable settings file gives `SettingsBroken`, and `send` in settings.ts:208-221 reports the error and returns without throwing. So when the user clicks "Don't start" in Settings, the servers stop, but the button stays on "Start", and at the next window focus `findAgain` applies the stored "start" (line 119) and starts them again. A failed "Start" does the reverse: servers run while the button says "Don't start". Every other settings action changes nothing in the window after a failed write. `changeAdded` (line 139) follows that rule by applying `storedAnswer`, so this is a second, conflicting copy of the rule for which answer is in force.
fix: After the write, apply what the settings now hold, the way `changeAdded` does: `const now = storedAnswer(setup)`, call `setSpecs([], …)` only when `now === "dontStart"`, then `apply(setup, now)`. Add a serverSetup.test.ts case where the fake `setServerAnswer` leaves the settings unchanged and expect the servers' states to stay as they were.
triage: block

problem: #974 Escape for every question now goes through the server set-up. App.vue sends QuestionDialog's `dismiss` to the store's `dismissQuestion`, which belongs to `ServerSetup`. It bumps a `dismissals` counter in serverSetup and calls `asking.answer(false)`; `ask()` (lines 93-97) then compares counters to tell Escape from "Don't start". The state table says `ui/asking.ts` owns the question waiting for an answer, but this lifecycle state now lives in a second module. The unsaved-changes, key-clash and Mark-resolved questions (exit/clash/unprocessed) depend on serverSetup for their Escape, and the next question that needs Escape to differ from cancel would need another counter.
fix: Give `asking.ts` a `dismiss()` and let a question resolve to dismissed, for example `ask` resolving `true | false | null` behind a small wrapper for the existing boolean callers. Bind QuestionDialog's `dismiss` to it, then delete `dismissals` and `dismissQuestion` from serverSetup. This needs asking.ts added to Owned.
triage: block (same fix as #966)

problem: #975 If the start `look` fails (`host.context()` or a detection IPC call rejects), `setUp` returns before `started = true`, so every later `findServers` does nothing for the rest of the run. That breaks #70's "looked for again whenever the window regains focus" after a single transient IPC failure. Today it is reachable only when the IPC itself rejects, because the Rust commands cannot fail. The test at serverSetup.test.ts:394 pins the start behaviour but has no focus case. As the app grows, any fallible lookup added to detection would inherit this one-strike rule without anyone noticing.
fix: Separate "the start flow has run" from "the start look succeeded": set `started` in a `finally` (or before the early return), so focus looks again without ever asking. Add a test where the first context call fails and a later `findServers` finds the servers stopped and asks nothing.
triage: promoted: one transient failure disables plan #70 focus detection for the run; untested rule
